docs.title: Memory CLI User Guide
docs.text:
The memory CLI is the command-line client for the Memory platform. It creates and selects projects, uploads documents, queries the knowledge graph, and manages the resources in a project.

This page is the operator-oriented walkthrough: install, authenticate, choose a project, and run the everyday commands. The exhaustive command listing lives in the CLI Reference; credential resolution details live in CLI Authentication.

docs.title: One-line installer (recommended)
docs.text:
The published install script detects the OS and architecture, downloads the latest release binary, installs it to ~/.memory/bin/memory, adds that directory to your shell PATH, and installs shell completions:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emergent-company/emergent.memory/main/deploy/install-cli.sh | bash

Pin a version by setting VERSION for the shell that runs the installer:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emergent-company/emergent.memory/main/deploy/install-cli.sh | VERSION=v0.88.8 bash

docs.title: Pre-built archive
docs.text:
Each release attaches CLI archives to GitHub Releases. Asset names follow memory-cli-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz (or .zip on Windows), for example:

curl -L -o memory-cli.tar.gz \
  https://github.com/emergent-company/emergent.memory/releases/latest/download/memory-cli-linux-amd64.tar.gz
tar xzf memory-cli.tar.gz
sudo mv memory-cli-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/memory

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
Requires Go 1.25+:

task cli:install          # installs to ~/.memory/bin/memory

Without task:

cd apps/cli
go build -o ~/.memory/bin/memory ./cmd/main.go

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text:
memory version

This prints the CLI version, commit hash, and build date. memory --version and memory -v are aliases.

docs.title: Authenticate
docs.text:
The CLI resolves credentials from three sources, highest priority first:

  1. A project token (emt_*) from MEMORY_PROJECT_API_KEY / MEMORY_PROJECT_TOKEN, the project_token config key, or --project-token
  2. An account API key from MEMORY_ACCOUNT_API_KEY / MEMORY_API_KEY
  3. An OAuth session stored in ~/.memory/credentials.json by memory login

docs.title: OAuth device flow: memory login
docs.text:
memory login

memory login starts the OAuth device authorization flow, prints a user code, opens the browser, and saves the resulting credentials to ~/.memory/credentials.json. Tokens refresh automatically. This is the right choice when one login should cover several projects.

If the server is running in standalone mode it has no OAuth issuer; use an API key or project token instead.

docs.title: Static bearer token: memory set-token
docs.text:
memory set-token <your-token>

memory set-token saves a pre-issued Bearer token to ~/.memory/credentials.json, bypassing the device flow. It is intended for CI, test harnesses, and environments that hand out tokens directly. The default validity is 24 hours; override it with --duration:

memory set-token <your-token> --duration 168h

Command path

set-token is a top-level command. The CLI does not have a memory auth command group, so memory auth set-token is not a valid invocation.

docs.title: Account API key (standalone / self-hosted)
docs.text:
export MEMORY_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3002
export MEMORY_ACCOUNT_API_KEY=<your-api-key>
memory status

Or persist it in the config file:

memory config set-server https://memory.example.com
memory config set api_key <your-api-key>

Secret values are not echoed back by memory config set.

docs.title: Check the session: memory status
docs.text:
memory status

memory status prints the authentication mode, server URL, a masked credential, connection health and server version, the active project (or a numbered list of projects to choose from), and usage statistics for the current project (documents, graph objects, relationships, type registry, template packs, and processing job queue depths).

docs.title: Sign out
docs.text:
memory logout          # remove the OAuth credentials file
memory logout --all    # also clear api_key and project_token from config

docs.title: Choose a project
docs.text:
Most commands need a project scope. There are four ways to supply it, in precedence order:

  1. --project <project-id> on the command (also available as a global flag)
  2. MEMORY_PROJECT — a project name or slug, resolved to an ID
  3. MEMORY_PROJECT_ID / project_id in ~/.memory/config.yaml
  4. A project token in .env.local or the config, which fixes the project server-side

docs.title: Interactive setup: memory init
docs.text:
cd my-project
memory init

memory init is an interactive wizard that:

  1. selects an existing project or creates a new one
  2. configures an LLM provider at the organisation level
  3. installs the built-in Memory skills into .agents/skills/

It writes MEMORY_PROJECT_ID, MEMORY_PROJECT_NAME, and MEMORY_PROJECT_API_KEY to .env.local (mode 0600) and adds .env.local to .gitignore. Running it again detects the existing configuration and offers to verify or reconfigure each step.

Flag Description --skip-provider Skip the LLM provider configuration step --skip-skills Skip the Memory skills installation step

memory init requires an interactive terminal; stdin must be a TTY.

docs.title: Pick a project directly
docs.text:
memory projects list                 # numbered list of accessible projects
memory projects list --stats         # include document/object/job counts
memory projects set "Product Research"
memory projects set --clear          # remove the active project from config

memory projects set updates project_id in ~/.memory/config.yaml and writes MEMORY_PROJECT_ID, MEMORY_PROJECT_NAME, and MEMORY_PROJECT_API_KEY into .env.local in the current directory. If no token exists for the project, it creates one.

docs.title: Ask the assistant: memory ask
docs.text:
memory ask "how do I ingest a PDF and query the resulting graph?"

memory ask is context-aware: without authentication it answers documentation questions, with an account it can run account-level tasks, and with an active project it can execute tasks against that project.

Flag Description --project <id> Project ID (uses the default project if omitted) --show-tools Show the tool calls made while answering --show-time Print elapsed time --json Emit JSON ({question, response, tools, elapsedMs}) --runtime <python\|go> Sandbox runtime for scripting tasks (default python) --v2 Use the v2 code-generation agent

Quotes are optional; the words after ask are joined into the question.

docs.title: Query the graph: memory query
docs.text:
memory query "what are the main services and how do they relate?"
memory query --mode=search "auth service"
memory query --mode=search --branch <branch-id> "planned services"

By default --mode=agent uses the server-side graph-query agent, which reasons over the knowledge graph with search and traversal tools. --mode=search runs a direct hybrid search without AI reasoning.

Flag Description --mode <agent\|search> Query mode (default agent) --project <id> Project to query --branch <branch-id> Search a graph branch (--mode=search only) --limit <n> Maximum results (--mode=search only, default 10) --result-types <graph\|text\|both> Result channels (--mode=search only) --fusion-strategy <weighted\|rrf\|interleave\|graph_first\|text_first> Fusion strategy (--mode=search only) --show-tools Show agent tool calls (--mode=agent only) --show-scores Print relevance scores (--mode=search only) --session <id> Continue a previous query session --json Emit JSON --show-time Print elapsed query time

To inspect individual objects instead of asking a question, use the graph commands:

memory graph objects list --type Person --limit 20
memory graph objects list --key user-alice
memory graph objects list --filter status=active --filter-op eq
memory graph objects get <id-or-key>
memory graph objects get <id-or-key> --branch <branch-id-or-name>
memory graph relationships list --type KNOWS --limit 20

Object creation:

memory graph objects create \
  --type Person \
  --name "Alice" \
  --properties '{"role":"engineer"}'
Flag Description --type <type> Object type (required) --name <name> Shorthand for a name property --description <text> Shorthand for a description property --properties <json> JSON properties object --key <key> Stable key for idempotent operations --status <status> Object status, e.g. active --branch <branch-id> Create on a branch instead of the main graph --upsert Update an existing object with the same --key

docs.title: Ingest documents: memory documents
docs.text:
memory documents upload ./report.pdf --auto-extract
memory documents upload ./report.pdf
memory documents list --limit 20
memory documents list --status extracted
memory documents get <document-id>
memory documents extraction-summary <document-id>
memory documents delete <document-id>
Command / flag Description upload <file> Upload a local file as a document --auto-extract Trigger extraction after upload list List documents; supports --limit, --cursor, --status, --sort, --order, --search, --source-type get <id> Print a document by ID extraction-summary <id> Show the extraction summary for a document delete <id> Delete the document and its related entities

memory documents upload prints the document ID, name, and status; if the file is a duplicate it prints the existing document ID instead.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
memory upgrade           # download and replace the CLI binary
memory upgrade --force   # upgrade even from a dev build

memory upgrade only touches the CLI binary. A self-hosted server installation is upgraded separately:

memory server upgrade

docs.title: Global flags and configuration
docs.text:
Flag Description --server <url> Memory server URL --project <id> Project ID (overrides config and environment) --project-token <token> Project token (overrides config and environment) --output <table\|json\|yaml\|csv> Output format (default table) --json Shorthand for --output json --config <path> Config file (default ~/.memory/config.yaml) --debug Enable debug logging --no-color Disable coloured output --compact Use compact output layout

The config file defaults to ~/.memory/config.yaml. Environment variables override the file, and flags override both:

server_url: https://memory.example.com
api_key: ''
project_token: ''
org_id: ''
project_id: ''
Environment variable Meaning MEMORY_SERVER_URL Server URL MEMORY_ACCOUNT_API_KEY Account-level API key MEMORY_PROJECT_API_KEY Project token (emt_*) MEMORY_PROJECT Project name or slug to activate MEMORY_PROJECT_ID Default project ID MEMORY_ORG_ID Default organisation ID MEMORY_CONFIG Override the config file path

Never commit credentials

Prefer environment variables or .env.local (which memory init writes with mode 0600) for tokens. Do not paste real tokens into scripts, screenshots, or documentation — use <your-token> placeholders.

docs.title: Python SDK
docs.text:
The Python SDK (emergent-memory) is a client library for the Memory API. It mirrors the Go SDK, exposes one root Client with a sub-client per resource area, and supports all three authentication modes plus SSE streaming.

Source: sdk/python/ Import name: emergent Distribution name: emergent-memory

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
PyPI publication

The package is not published on PyPI yet. The release workflow (python-sdk-release.yml) publishes to PyPI when a python-sdk/v* tag is pushed, so pip install emergent-memory is the intended install command once the first release is out. Until then, install from source.

From a clone of the repository:

git clone https://github.com/emergent-company/emergent.memory.git
cd emergent.memory
pip install -e sdk/python

Runtime requirements, from sdk/python/pyproject.toml:

Requirement Version Python >=3.10 httpx >=0.24.0 pydantic >=2.0.0

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from emergent import Client

client = Client.from_api_key("https://memory.emergent-company.ai", "<your-token>")
client.set_context(org_id="org_abc123", project_id="proj_xyz789")

for project in client.projects.list():
    print(project["id"], project["name"])

client.close()

Use the client as a context manager to close the HTTP connection pool automatically:

from emergent import Client

with Client.from_api_key("https://memory.emergent-company.ai", "<your-token>") as client:
    client.set_context(org_id="org_abc123", project_id="proj_xyz789")
    print(client.documents.list(limit=10))

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Client sends one of two credential headers, depending on the mode:

Mode Use it for Header sent apikey Standalone / self-hosted server key X-API-Key: <key> apitoken Project-scoped token (emt_*) Authorization: Bearer <token> oauth OAuth 2.0 access token you manage Authorization: Bearer <token>

mode="apikey" is the default. If the key starts with emt_, the SDK detects it and switches to APITokenProvider automatically, so the same constructor works for a server key and a project token.

from emergent import Client

# Standalone server API key (X-API-Key)
client = Client.from_api_key("http://localhost:3012", "<server-api-key>")

# Project API token (emt_ prefix -> Bearer, auto-detected)
client = Client.from_api_key("https://memory.emergent-company.ai", "emt_<your-token>")

# OAuth access token (the caller refreshes it)
client = Client.from_oauth_token(
    "https://memory.emergent-company.ai",
    access_token="<your-access-token>",
)

docs.title: Automatic discovery with Client.from_env()
docs.text:
from emergent import Client

client = Client.from_env()

Configuration is merged in this order, lowest priority first:

  1. ~/.memory/config.yaml (server_url, api_key, project_token, org_id, project_id)
  2. .env (walked up from the current directory)
  3. .env.local (walked up from the current directory)
  4. MEMORY_* environment variables

Recognised environment variables:

Variable Meaning MEMORY_SERVER_URL Server URL (MEMORY_API_URL is an alias) MEMORY_ACCOUNT_API_KEY Account-level key (MEMORY_API_KEY is a deprecated alias) MEMORY_PROJECT_API_KEY Project token (MEMORY_PROJECT_TOKEN is a deprecated alias) MEMORY_ORG_ID Default organisation ID MEMORY_PROJECT_ID Default project ID

If MEMORY_PROJECT_API_KEY is set, it is used as the credential instead of the account key. from_env() raises OSError when no server URL or credential can be found.

docs.title: Full configuration object
docs.text:
from emergent import Client, Config

client = Client(
    Config(
        server_url="https://memory.emergent-company.ai",
        api_key="emt_<your-token>",
        org_id="org_abc123",
        project_id="proj_xyz789",
    )
)

Config fields: server_url (required), api_key, mode, access_token, org_id, project_id, and an optional http_client.

docs.title: Organisation and project context
docs.text:
Most sub-clients send X-Org-ID and X-Project-ID on every request. Set both once; set_context propagates the values to every context-scoped sub-client atomically.

client.set_context(org_id="org_abc123", project_id="proj_xyz789")

If you manage the HTTP transport yourself, authenticate_request injects the same auth and context headers into a plain dict:

headers = client.authenticate_request({})
# {"Authorization": "Bearer <token>", "X-Org-ID": "...", "X-Project-ID": "..."}

docs.title: Projects and organisations
docs.text:
These sub-clients are not project-scoped.

projects = client.projects.list()
project = client.projects.get("proj_xyz789")

created = client.projects.create({"name": "Product Research"})
client.projects.update("proj_xyz789", {"name": "Renamed"})
client.projects.delete("proj_xyz789")

orgs = client.orgs.list()
org = client.orgs.get("org_abc123")
client.orgs.create({"name": "Acme Corp"})
client.orgs.delete("org_abc123")

docs.title: Knowledge graph
docs.text:
Objects are created from a payload and returned as dictionaries.

obj = client.graph.create_object(
    {
        "type": "Person",
        "name": "Alice",
        "properties": {"role": "engineer"},
    }
)

obj = client.graph.get_object(obj["id"])
client.graph.update_object(obj["id"], {"properties": {"role": "lead"}})
client.graph.delete_object(obj["id"])

page = client.graph.list_objects(type="Person", limit=50)
count = client.graph.count_objects(type="Person")

Upserts and search:

client.graph.upsert_object(
    {
        "externalId": "user-alice",
        "type": "Person",
        "name": "Alice",
    }
)

hits = client.graph.fts_search("Alice", limit=20)
similar = client.graph.find_similar(obj["id"], limit=10)

# Hybrid search with graph neighbours, and subgraph extraction, take a payload
res = client.graph.search_with_neighbors({"query": "machine learning", "limit": 5})
sub = client.graph.subgraph({"object_ids": [obj["id"]], "depth": 2})

Relationships take a payload with type, src_id, and dst_id. Optional keys include properties, weight, and branch_id.

rel = client.graph.create_relationship(
    {
        "type": "KNOWS",
        "src_id": "obj_1",
        "dst_id": "obj_2",
        "properties": {"since": "2024"},
    }
)

client.graph.list_relationships(type="KNOWS", limit=50)
client.graph.count_relationships(type="KNOWS")
client.graph.get_relationship_history(rel["id"])
client.graph.restore_relationship(rel["id"])

Objects can be moved between branches:

client.graph.move_object("obj_id", target_branch_id="branch_2")

docs.title: Documents
docs.text:
docs = client.documents.list(limit=50, offset=0)
doc = client.documents.get("doc_id")

# Upload a local file; extraction is enabled by default
result = client.documents.upload("/path/to/report.pdf", auto_extract=True)

# Signed download URL (the server redirects; this returns the target)
url = client.documents.download_url("doc_id")

client.documents.bulk_delete(["doc_1", "doc_2"])
summary = client.documents.get_extraction_summary("doc_id")

upload() returns {"document": ..., "isDuplicate": bool, "existingDocumentId": ...}. Pass file_name="..." to override the uploaded file name.

docs.title: Unified search
docs.text:
results = client.search.search(
    "machine learning",
    limit=10,
    strategy="hybrid",
    result_types="both",
)

graph_only = client.search.graph_search("neural networks", limit=5)
text_only = client.search.text_search("neural networks", limit=5)

search() returns {"results": [...], "metadata": {...}}; the two convenience methods return the result list directly.

docs.title: Chat and streaming
docs.text:
chat.stream() is a generator of typed SSE events. The message is the first positional argument.

from emergent import Client, DoneEvent, MetaEvent, TokenEvent

with Client.from_api_key("https://memory.emergent-company.ai", "<your-token>") as client:
    client.set_context(org_id="org_abc123", project_id="proj_xyz789")

    for event in client.chat.stream("What is a knowledge graph?"):
        if isinstance(event, TokenEvent):
            print(event.token, end="", flush=True)
        elif isinstance(event, MetaEvent):
            print("\nCitations:", event.citations)
        elif isinstance(event, DoneEvent):
            break

Continue an existing conversation with conversation_id:

conv = client.chat.create_conversation(title="My chat", message="Hello")
for event in client.chat.stream("Summarise the graph", conversation_id=conv.id):
    if event.type == "token":
        print(event.token, end="")

chat.ask() streams an answer through the project ask endpoint, and chat.ask_collect() blocks and returns the accumulated text as a string:

answer = client.chat.ask_collect("Summarise the project goals")
print(answer)

for event in client.chat.ask("Summarise project goals"):
    if event.type == "token":
        print(event.token, end="")

SSE event classes:

Class type Key attributes MetaEvent "meta" conversation_id, citations, graph_objects TokenEvent "token" token (text delta) MCPToolEvent "mcp_tool" tool, status, result, error ErrorEvent "error" error DoneEvent "done" — UnknownEvent any other value raw

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
agents = client.agents.list()
agent = client.agents.get("agent_id")

run = client.agents.trigger("agent_id")
run = client.agents.get_project_run(run["runId"])

client.agents.respond_to_question("<question-id>", "yes")

docs.title: Other sub-clients
docs.text: Attribute Purpose client.branches List, create, update, fork, and delete graph branches client.tasks Project and cross-project background tasks client.schemas Schema packs: list available/installed, assign client.skills Project skills CRUD client.agent_definitions Agent definition templates client.api_tokens Project and account API tokens client.mcp MCP JSON-RPC client (list_tools, call_tool, ...)

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
HTTP errors are raised as APIError. The exception carries status_code, code, message, and details, plus predicate properties:

from emergent import APIError

try:
    obj = client.graph.get_object("nonexistent")
except APIError as e:
    if e.is_not_found:
        print("Object not found")
    elif e.is_unauthorized:
        print("Check the credential")
    else:
        print(f"API error {e.status_code}: {e.message}")

Other exported exceptions are EmergentError (base class), AuthError, and StreamError.

docs.title: Closing the client
docs.text:
client.close()

If you supplied http_client in Config, the SDK does not close it; you own that client's lifecycle.
