docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text:
This guide covers topics for developers integrating with, extending, or operating the Memory platform.

  • Provider Setup

    Configure LLM providers (Google AI, Vertex AI) at the org or project level. Manage API keys, model overrides, and track token usage and costs.

  • MCP Servers

    Register external MCP servers (stdio, SSE, HTTP) and the built-in Memory MCP server. Browse the official MCP registry and install community servers.

  • Extraction Pipeline

    Monitor and control extraction jobs that turn documents into graph objects. View per-job logs including LLM calls, token counts, and created objects.

  • Email Setup

    Configure Mailgun to enable transactional email (invitations, notifications). Understand the async job queue and delivery tracking.

  • Health & Ops

    Health check endpoints, the diagnostics probe, debug stats, and the auto-generated OpenAPI spec.

  • Security Scopes

    Complete reference for all 38 permission scopes, umbrella scope expansions, and which scopes are assignable to API tokens.

  • CLI Reference

    Reference for memory init, memory ask, memory adk-sessions, memory mcp-guide, and memory install-memory-skills.

docs.title: CLI Authentication
docs.text:
The memory CLI supports three credential sources. It picks the first one that is set, in this order:

Priority Mode Environment Config key Scope 1 Project token (emt_…) MEMORY_PROJECT_API_KEY, MEMORY_PROJECT_TOKEN project_token one project 2 Account API key / standalone key MEMORY_ACCOUNT_API_KEY, MEMORY_API_KEY api_key account / org 3 OAuth session memory login → ~/.memory/credentials.json — account, with project selection

memory status prints which mode is active, the server URL, a masked credential, and connection health.

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
Defaults to ~/.memory/config.yaml; override the path with MEMORY_CONFIG.

server_url: https://memory.example.com
api_key: ''          # account-level key
project_token: ''    # emt_… project token
project_id: ''
org_id: ''

Environment variables win over the file. MEMORY_PROJECT selects a project by name or slug; MEMORY_SERVER_URL overrides server_url.

docs.title: OAuth (interactive, full server)
docs.text:
memory login      # device flow; stores credentials in ~/.memory/credentials.json
memory status     # shows the active project, or a numbered list to pick from

Tokens refresh automatically. Use this when you want one login to cover several projects without pasting keys.

docs.title: Project token vs account key
docs.text:
Project tokens are scoped to a single project and are the right credential for CI that operates on one project. Some commands are account- or org-level (listing projects, managing account tokens); with only a project token configured they fail with:

account-level credentials required for this command.

Fix: run memory login, or set MEMORY_ACCOUNT_API_KEY to an account-level key.

docs.title: Standalone servers (API key only)
docs.text:
A self-hosted server started with STANDALONE_API_KEY accepts that key as an account credential — no Zitadel, no OAuth:

export MEMORY_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3002   # self-hosted default (SERVER_PORT)
export MEMORY_ACCOUNT_API_KEY=<STANDALONE_API_KEY from the server .env>

memory status

docs.title: CI example
docs.text:
- name: Query the graph
  env:
    MEMORY_SERVER_URL: ${{ vars.MEMORY_SERVER_URL }}
    MEMORY_PROJECT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.MEMORY_PROJECT_TOKEN }}
  run: memory query "Which documents were added this week?"

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause 401 / not authenticated No credential resolved — set a token or run memory login 403 Insufficient permissions on an account command A project token is configured; use an account key or OAuth Config file seems ignored An environment variable is set and takes priority Wrong project MEMORY_PROJECT, project_id in the config file, or memory status to switch

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
The memory CLI provides commands for setting up projects, querying the knowledge graph, and managing AI agent integrations. This page documents commands that are not covered elsewhere in the developer guide.

See memory --help for the full list of available commands and global flags.

docs.title: memory init
docs.text:
Interactive wizard that configures a Memory project in the current directory.

What it does

Walks through three steps:

  1. Project — select an existing project or create a new one
  2. Provider — configure an LLM provider at the org level (e.g., Google AI, Vertex AI)
  3. Skills — install the built-in Memory skills into .agents/skills/

On completion it writes the following variables to .env.local and automatically adds .env.local to .gitignore:

Variable Description MEMORY_PROJECT_ID UUID of the configured project MEMORY_PROJECT_NAME Human-readable project name MEMORY_PROJECT_API_KEY Project-scoped API token

Running memory init again in an already-configured directory detects the existing configuration and offers to verify or reconfigure each step.

Flags

Flag Description --skip-provider Skip the LLM provider configuration step --skip-skills Skip the Memory skills installation step

Example

cd my-project
memory init

docs.title: memory ask
docs.text:
Ask the Memory CLI assistant a question or request a task. The assistant is context-aware and adapts based on your authentication state and whether a project is configured.

Context modes

State Behaviour Not authenticated Documentation answers; explains how to log in Authenticated, no project Account-level tasks + documentation answers Authenticated + project active Full task execution + documentation answers

The assistant fetches live documentation from the Memory docs site to answer questions about the CLI, SDK, REST API, agents, and knowledge graph features. It can also execute tasks on your behalf.

Examples

memory ask "what are native tools?"
memory ask "what agents do I have configured?"
memory ask "how do I create a schema?"
memory ask --project abc123 "list all agent runs from today"
memory ask "what commands are available for managing API tokens?"

Flags

Flag Description --project <id> Project ID (uses default project if omitted) --json Output result as JSON {question, response, tools, elapsedMs} --show-tools Show tool calls made by the assistant during reasoning --show-time Show elapsed time at the end of the response --runtime <python\|go> Sandbox runtime for scripting tasks (default: python) --v2 Use the v2 code-generation agent (fewer round-trips, faster)

docs.title: memory adk-sessions
docs.text:
Alias: memory sessions

Manage and inspect Google ADK (Agent Development Kit) sessions. ADK sessions represent individual agent conversation threads, including the full event history of messages and tool calls.

docs.title: memory adk-sessions list
docs.text:
List all ADK sessions for the active project.

memory adk-sessions list
memory adk-sessions list --project <id>
memory adk-sessions list --json

Output per session: ID: <id> | App: <app> | User: <user> | Updated: <timestamp>

docs.title: memory adk-sessions get
docs.text:
Get full details and the complete event history for a specific session. Outputs the full session record as indented JSON including all events (user messages, agent responses, tool calls).

memory adk-sessions get <session-id>
memory sessions get <session-id> --project <id>

docs.title: memory mcp-guide
docs.text:
Print ready-to-use MCP server configuration snippets for connecting AI agents to Memory.

Outputs JSON configuration blocks for Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible clients. Snippets use the active server URL and API key (project token takes precedence over account key).

memory mcp-guide

Copy the relevant block into your AI client's MCP configuration to enable Memory tools. For Claude Desktop the output corresponds to the entry in ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json.

docs.title: memory install-memory-skills
docs.text:
Install the built-in Memory skills from the embedded catalog into .agents/skills/ in the current directory (or a custom directory).

Memory skills are instruction files that teach AI agents (Claude, GPT-4, etc.) how to use the Memory CLI and platform. By default, only skills with the memory- prefix are installed.

Flags

Flag Description --dir <path> Target directory (default: .agents/skills relative to cwd) --force Overwrite existing skill directories

Examples

# Install into the default .agents/skills/ directory
memory install-memory-skills

# Install into a custom directory
memory install-memory-skills --dir ./my-agent/skills

# Re-install / update all skills, overwriting existing ones
memory install-memory-skills --force

Existing skill directories are skipped by default. Use --force to update them to the latest embedded versions.

docs.title: memory agents mcp-servers import
docs.text:
Import MCP servers from a Claude-format config document (mcpServers).

Flags

Flag Description --from-claude <path|-> Claude config file, or - for stdin (required) --device <instance-id> Connector instance for device-targeted (stdio) servers --target <auto\|server\|device> Delivery target (default auto) --overwrite Update servers whose name already exists instead of skipping --dry-run Validate and plan without writing --json Emit the per-entry result as JSON

auto creates remote http/sse servers on the Memory host and pushes local stdio servers to the connector named by --device. ${VAR} placeholders are stored literally.

Example

memory agents mcp-servers import --from-claude ~/.claude.json --device laptop-connector
cat claude_desktop_config.json | memory agents mcp-servers import --from-claude - --dry-run

docs.title: Email Setup
docs.text: Memory sends transactional emails for events such as org invitations and workspace notifications. Email is delivered via Mailgun using a background job queue with automatic retries and delivery tracking.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The email subsystem is entirely background-based — there are no REST endpoints. Other parts of the server (e.g. the invitations domain) enqueue email jobs, and a polling worker processes them asynchronously.

Application code
      │ enqueue EmailJob
      ▼
kb.email_jobs (Postgres queue)
      │
      ▼
Email worker (polls every ~5s)
      │ renders Handlebars template
      ▼
Mailgun API
      │
      ▼
Recipient inbox

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set the following environment variables on the server:

Variable Required Description EMAIL_ENABLED Yes Set to true to enable email sending MAILGUN_DOMAIN Yes Your Mailgun sending domain, e.g. mg.example.com MAILGUN_API_KEY Yes Mailgun private API key MAILGUN_SIGNING_KEY No Mailgun HTTP webhook signing key, required for delivery tracking. Found in the Mailgun control panel under Settings → API keys → HTTP webhook signing key. Without it, every delivery-status webhook is rejected fail-closed and delivery_status never updates EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS Yes Sender email address, e.g. noreply@example.com EMAIL_FROM_NAME No Sender display name, e.g. Memory Platform MAILGUN_API_BASE No Override the Mailgun API base URL, including the /v3 segment (e.g. a local stub). Defaults to the SDK US base, or the EU base when MAILGUN_REGION=eu EMAIL_TEMPLATE_DIR No Path to Handlebars email templates (defaults to templates/email)

When MAILGUN_DOMAIN or MAILGUN_API_KEY are absent or empty, the email system falls back to a no-op sender that logs all emails without sending them. This is the default in development.

docs.title: Verifying email is configured
docs.text:
Check the server startup logs for:

INFO  email: configured (domain=mg.example.com, from=noreply@example.com)

Or the no-op fallback:

WARN  email: not configured — using no-op sender (emails will be logged only)

docs.title: Email job lifecycle
docs.text:
Each job transitions through these statuses:

Status Description pending Waiting to be processed processing Worker has picked it up sent Successfully delivered to Mailgun failed Send failed; will retry dead_letter Max attempts reached; will not retry

Failed jobs use exponential backoff starting from 60 seconds. After 3 attempts (configurable), the job moves to dead_letter.

docs.title: Delivery tracking
docs.text:
Mailgun delivers delivery events (bounces, complaints, failures, deliveries) by POSTing them to the server's public webhook POST /api/webhooks/mailgun. Each request is HMAC-verified against MAILGUN_SIGNING_KEY; only validly signed events are recorded in kb.email_logs and reconciled to the originating kb.email_jobs row.

Delivery status Description pending Email accepted by Mailgun, not yet delivered delivered Delivered to recipient mail server opened Recipient opened the email clicked Recipient clicked a link bounced Hard bounce (invalid address) soft_bounced Temporary delivery failure complained Marked as spam by recipient unsubscribed Recipient unsubscribed failed Delivery definitively failed

docs.title: Email templates
docs.text:
Templates are Handlebars (.hbs) files in the template directory. Each email type maps to a template name. Template variables are passed as templateData when the job is enqueued by application code.

Example template structure:

templates/email/
  invite.hbs
  workspace-ready.hbs
  password-reset.hbs

docs.title: Email job entity reference
docs.text:
EmailJob — table kb.email_jobs

Field Type Description id UUID Primary key templateName string Handlebars template to render toEmail string Recipient email address toName string Recipient display name (optional) subject string Email subject line templateData object Key-value data passed to the template status string See lifecycle table above attempts int Number of send attempts maxAttempts int Max retries (default 3) lastError string Last failure message mailgunMessageId string Mailgun message ID on success deliveryStatus string Mailgun delivery event status sourceType string Originating domain label, e.g. invite sourceId UUID Originating record ID createdAt timestamp processedAt timestamp When the job was finalized nextRetryAt timestamp Earliest time to retry

docs.title: Worker configuration
docs.text:
The email worker polls for pending jobs every 5 seconds and processes up to 10 jobs per batch. These values are tuneable via server configuration but cannot be changed at runtime without a restart.

Setting Default Description workerIntervalMs 5000 Polling interval in milliseconds workerBatchSize 10 Jobs dequeued per poll tick maxRetries 3 Max send attempts per job retryDelaySec 60 Base retry delay (exponential backoff)

docs.title: Extraction Pipeline
docs.text: The extraction pipeline turns raw documents into structured knowledge graph objects. It runs asynchronously across multiple job queues and exposes an admin API for monitoring and control.

docs.title: How extraction works
docs.text:
Document uploaded
      │
      ▼
Document parsing job   ← chunks text into passages
      │
      ▼
Object extraction job  ← LLM extracts typed objects + relationships
      │
      ▼
Chunk embedding jobs   ← embeds document chunks for search
      │
      ▼
Graph embedding jobs   ← embeds extracted objects for vector search

Each stage is an independent job queue. Failures in one stage don't block others.

docs.title: Job types
docs.text: Job type jobType value Description Full extraction full_extraction Process all chunks in a document Re-extraction reextraction Re-process an already-extracted document Incremental incremental Process only new/changed chunks

docs.title: Job statuses
docs.text: API status Description queued Waiting to be picked up running Currently processing completed Successfully finished failed Failed after max retries cancelled Manually cancelled requires_review Completed but flagged for human review

docs.title: Trigger types
docs.text: Trigger triggerType value Description Manual manual Created via API Scheduled scheduled Created by the scheduler Webhook webhook Triggered by a datasource sync event

docs.title: List jobs for a project
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs/projects/<projectId> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Query parameters:

Parameter Description status Filter by status: queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled jobType Filter by job type limit Number of results (default 20) offset Pagination offset

docs.title: Get a specific job
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs/<jobId> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Get job statistics
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs/projects/<projectId>/statistics \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Returns counts by status and job type, plus throughput metrics (jobs per hour, average duration).

docs.title: Create a job manually
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "projectId": "<projectId>",
    "documentId": "<documentId>",
    "jobType": "full_extraction",
    "priority": 10
  }'

Higher priority values are processed first.

docs.title: Cancel a job
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs/<jobId>/cancel \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Retry a failed job
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs/<jobId>/retry \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Bulk cancel
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs/projects/<projectId>/bulk-cancel \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status": "queued"}'

docs.title: Bulk retry
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs/projects/<projectId>/bulk-retry \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status": "failed"}'

docs.title: Bulk delete
docs.text:
curl -X DELETE https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs/projects/<projectId>/bulk-delete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"status": "completed", "olderThanDays": 30}'

docs.title: Job logs
docs.text: Each extraction job records detailed logs for every step, including LLM calls, token counts, and objects created.

docs.title: Get logs for a job
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/extraction-jobs/<jobId>/logs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Log entry fields
docs.text: Field Description operation Type of step (see below) message Human-readable description metadata Structured context: model name, token counts, object IDs, etc. createdAt Timestamp

docs.title: Log operation types
docs.text: Operation Description llm_call An LLM was called — metadata includes model, input tokens, output tokens chunk_processing A document chunk was processed object_creation A graph object was created from extracted data relationship_creation A graph relationship was created suggestion_creation A suggestion (pending review) was created validation Schema validation was run on extracted data error An error occurred during processing

docs.title: Extraction job entity reference
docs.text:
ObjectExtractionJob — table kb.object_extraction_jobs

Field Type Description id UUID Primary key projectId UUID Owning project documentId UUID Source document (nullable) datasourceId UUID Source datasource (nullable) jobType string full_extraction | reextraction | incremental triggerType string manual | scheduled | webhook status string See status table above priority int Processing priority (higher = first) errorMsg string Last error message retryCount int Number of retries so far maxRetries int Maximum allowed retries startedAt timestamp When processing began completedAt timestamp When processing finished createdAt timestamp updatedAt timestamp

docs.title: Embedding control (ops)
docs.text:
Internal endpoints

These endpoints have no authentication. They must be protected at the network or firewall level.

docs.title: Check embedding worker status
docs.text: curl http://localhost:3012/api/embeddings/status

docs.title: Pause embedding worker
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:3012/api/embeddings/pause

Useful during maintenance windows or when running bulk re-indexing.

docs.title: Resume embedding worker
docs.text: curl -X POST http://localhost:3012/api/embeddings/resume

docs.title: Update embedding config
docs.text:
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3012/api/embeddings/config \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"batchSize": 50, "concurrency": 4}'

docs.title: Health & Ops
docs.text: The server exposes health check, readiness, diagnostics, and debug endpoints for use by load balancers, Kubernetes probes, and on-call engineers.

docs.title: Endpoints overview
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Auth GET /health Full health status with checks None GET /healthz Minimal liveness probe None GET /ready Readiness probe None GET /debug Go runtime stats (dev only) superadmin_full GET /api/diagnostics Deep DB diagnostics superadmin_full

The liveness/readiness probes (/health, /healthz, /ready) are deliberately unauthenticated so load balancers and Kubernetes probes can reach them. The internal diagnostic surfaces (/debug, /api/diagnostics) expose platform-tier internals (DB connection target, pool state, pg_stat_activity) and are gated on an active superadmin_full grant (the core.superadmins role), never a token scope and never a bare admin scope.

docs.title: /health — Full health check
docs.text:
Returns a JSON object with overall status and per-subsystem checks.

curl https://api.example.com/health

{
  "status": "healthy",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-08T12:00:00Z",
  "uptime": "3h12m5s",
  "version": "1.2.3",
  "checks": {
    "database": "healthy"
  }
}

Returns 200 when healthy. Returns 503 Service Unavailable when any check fails.

docs.title: /healthz — Minimal liveness probe
docs.text:
Returns plain text OK (200) or Service Unavailable (503). Use this for high-frequency Kubernetes liveness probes where JSON parsing overhead is undesirable.

curl https://api.example.com/healthz
# OK

docs.title: /ready — Readiness probe
docs.text:
Returns a JSON object indicating whether the server is ready to receive traffic. The server may be alive (/healthz) but not yet ready (e.g. still running migrations).

curl https://api.example.com/ready

{ "status": "ready" }

or

{ "status": "not_ready", "message": "database migrations pending" }

docs.title: /debug — Runtime stats
docs.text:
Development only

This endpoint is only available when the server is started in development mode. Do not expose it in production.

Requires an active superadmin_full grant. Returns Go runtime memory statistics and database connection pool stats as JSON.

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <superadmin-token>" http://localhost:3012/debug

{
  "go_runtime": {
    "goroutines": 42,
    "heap_alloc_mb": 128,
    "heap_sys_mb": 256,
    "gc_runs": 15
  },
  "db_pool": {
    "open_connections": 8,
    "in_use": 2,
    "idle": 6,
    "wait_count": 0
  }
}

docs.title: /api/diagnostics — Deep diagnostics
docs.text:
The diagnostics endpoint provides live database pool inspection and slow-query detection. Useful for on-call investigation of performance issues.

Requires an active superadmin_full grant. The long_queries report redacts raw SQL text — it exposes only the query length (query_length) alongside pid, duration, and state, so an in-flight query's literals (which may embed secrets or user data) never leave the server.

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <superadmin-token>" https://api.example.com/api/diagnostics

Response fields:

Field Description db_pool Bun connection pool statistics pg_stat_activity Active Postgres sessions from pg_stat_activity long_queries Queries running longer than 5 seconds settings Relevant PostgreSQL configuration settings table_sizes Top tables by disk size

Example response:

{
  "db_pool": {
    "open_connections": 10,
    "in_use": 3,
    "idle": 7
  },
  "pg_stat_activity": [
    {
      "pid": 1234,
      "state": "active",
      "query_length": 42,
      "duration_sec": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "long_queries": [],
  "settings": {
    "max_connections": "100",
    "shared_buffers": "128MB"
  },
  "table_sizes": [
    { "table": "kb.graph_objects", "size": "4210 MB" },
    { "table": "kb.chunks", "size": "1024 MB" }
  ]
}

docs.title: OpenAPI specification
docs.text:
The server auto-generates an OpenAPI 3.0 specification. Access it at:

GET /api/docs/openapi.json

or in the admin UI:

https://admin.example.com/api-reference

You can import the spec into Postman, Insomnia, or any OpenAPI-compatible tool.

docs.title: Kubernetes probe configuration
docs.text:
Recommended Kubernetes probe settings:

livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 3012
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 3

readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /ready
    port: 3012
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 3

docs.title: Monitoring integration
docs.text:
For production monitoring, consider:

  • Uptime monitoring — poll /healthz every 30s from an external probe
  • Alerting — alert when /health returns non-healthy checks
  • Performance — use /api/diagnostics to investigate slow queries when latency spikes
  • Tracing — set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to enable OpenTelemetry tracing (no-op when unset)

docs.title: MCP Relay
docs.text: The MCP relay lets a remote process (e.g. an AI agent running on a separate machine) expose its local MCP tools to a Memory project via a persistent WebSocket connection. Memory acts as the relay hub — the agent registers its tools once, and any caller (another agent, the CLI, or a direct API call) can invoke those tools through Memory without needing direct network access to the remote process.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Remote agent  ──WebSocket──►  Memory relay hub  ◄──REST──  Caller (CLI / agent)
  (provider)                  /api/mcp-relay/               (consumer)
  1. The remote agent opens a WebSocket to /api/mcp-relay/connect?projectId=<id>.
  2. It sends a register frame advertising its instance ID and tool list.
  3. Memory stores the live session in memory and exposes it via REST.
  4. Any caller can list sessions, inspect tools, and forward tool calls — Memory proxies the request over the WebSocket and returns the response.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
GET /api/mcp-relay/connect?projectId=<projectId>
Authorization: Bearer <api_token>
Upgrade: websocket

docs.title: Frame types
docs.text: Frame Direction Description register provider → hub First frame after connecting. Advertises instance ID and tools. registered hub → provider Acknowledgement after successful registration. call hub → provider Hub forwards a tool invocation. response provider → hub Provider returns the tool result. ping provider → hub Keepalive ping. pong hub → provider Keepalive reply. error hub → provider Protocol error (e.g. malformed register frame).

docs.title: Register frame
docs.text:
{
  "type": "register",
  "instance_id": "my-agent-v1",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "tools": {
    "tools": [
      {
        "name": "search_codebase",
        "description": "Search the local codebase",
        "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": {} }
      }
    ]
  }
}

instance_id must be unique per project. If a session with the same ID is already connected it will be replaced when the new connection registers.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: All REST endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <api_token> and a projectId query parameter (or project context from a project-scoped token).

docs.title: List sessions
docs.text:
GET /api/mcp-relay/sessions?projectId=<id>

Returns all currently connected relay instances for the project.

{
  "sessions": [
    {
      "instance_id": "my-agent-v1",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "tool_count": 3,
      "connected_at": "2025-04-26T10:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Get tools for an instance
docs.text:
GET /api/mcp-relay/sessions/{instanceId}/tools?projectId=<id>

Returns the raw tools/list payload advertised by the relay instance.

docs.title: Call a tool
docs.text:
POST /api/mcp-relay/sessions/{instanceId}/call?projectId=<id>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "search_codebase",
  "arguments": { "query": "auth middleware" }
}

Memory forwards the call over the WebSocket and returns the result once the provider responds (default timeout: 30 s).

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
# List connected relay instances
memory mcp-relay sessions

# Show tools for a specific instance
memory mcp-relay tools <instance-id>

# Call a tool on a relay instance
memory mcp-relay call <instance-id> <tool-name>
memory mcp-relay call <instance-id> <tool-name> --args '{"query":"auth"}'

All commands respect the standard --project / MEMORY_PROJECT_ID context.

docs.title: Implementing a relay provider
docs.text:
A minimal relay provider in pseudocode:

import websocket, json

ws = websocket.connect(
    f"{MEMORY_URL}/api/mcp-relay/connect?projectId={PROJECT_ID}",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_TOKEN}"}
)

# 1. Register
ws.send(json.dumps({
    "type": "register",
    "instance_id": "my-agent",
    "tools": {"tools": [{"name": "ping", "description": "Ping", "inputSchema": {}}]}
}))

ack = json.loads(ws.recv())  # {"type":"registered","instance_id":"my-agent"}

# 2. Handle incoming calls
while True:
    msg = json.loads(ws.recv())
    if msg["type"] == "call":
        result = handle_tool(msg["params"]["name"], msg["params"].get("arguments", {}))
        ws.send(json.dumps({
            "type": "response",
            "id": msg["id"],
            "result": result
        }))
    elif msg["type"] == "ping":
        ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "pong"}))

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Sessions are in-memory only — a server restart clears all relay sessions.
  • The relay hub enforces a 30-second call timeout. Providers must respond within that window.
  • The WebSocket connection is kept alive via ping/pong. Providers should send a ping frame at least every 60 seconds to avoid the idle timeout.

docs.title: MCP Servers
docs.text:
Memory integrates with the Model Context Protocol in two ways:

  1. Built-in MCP server — Memory itself is an MCP server. Clients like Claude Desktop or Cursor connect directly to Memory to read/write the knowledge graph.
  2. MCP registry — Per-project registry of external MCP servers that agents can call as tools.

docs.title: Built-in Memory MCP server
docs.text:
Memory is a remote MCP server: there is no local stdio subcommand to run. The current spec transport is Streamable HTTP at /api/mcp; the project-scoped SSE endpoints remain available for clients that speak only SSE.

Transport Endpoint Authentication Streamable HTTP (spec 2025-11-25, recommended) /api/mcp — POST for JSON-RPC, GET for the server-initiated stream, DELETE to end the session X-API-Key: <api_token> + X-Project-ID: <project_id>, or Authorization: Bearer <api_token> SSE (legacy, project-scoped) GET /api/mcp/sse/<projectId>, POST /api/mcp/sse/<projectId>/message X-API-Key, Authorization: Bearer, or ?token=<api_token> JSON-RPC over HTTP (legacy) POST /api/mcp/rpc same token, as X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer

Send the project id as the X-Project-ID header on /api/mcp; the SSE routes carry it in the path instead.

Tip: memory mcp-guide prints these snippets for your server URL, with the token redacted to ${MEMORY_PROJECT_TOKEN} (pass --show-secret to inline the real value). It uses your first project, so check the X-Project-ID value before pasting if you belong to more than one.

docs.title: Connecting Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Add to ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memory": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.example.com/api/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-Project-ID": "<project-id>",
        "X-API-Key": "<your-api-token>"
      }
    }
  }
}

Clients that only implement the older SSE transport use the project-scoped endpoint instead — the project id is part of the URL there:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "memory": {
      "type": "sse",
      "url": "https://api.example.com/api/mcp/sse/<project-id>",
      "headers": {
        "X-API-Key": "<your-api-token>"
      }
    }
  }
}

A client that can only speak Authorization: Bearer works too: the same token is accepted in that header. Clients that only support stdio need their own documented bridge to a remote server — Memory does not ship a stdio mode.

docs.title: Connecting OpenCode
docs.text:
Add to opencode.json in your project directory:

{
  "mcp": {
    "memory": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://api.example.com/api/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-Project-ID": "<project-id>",
        "X-API-Key": "<your-api-token>"
      },
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}

Replace <project-id> with your project UUID (memory projects list) and <your-api-token> with a project-scoped API token. Run opencode mcp list to verify the connection.

docs.title: Available MCP tools (built-in)
docs.text:
The built-in server exposes tools including:

  • Knowledge graph — create, update, search objects and relationships
  • Documents — upload, list, retrieve documents
  • Search — unified vector + keyword search
  • Chat — create sessions, send messages
  • Agents — list agents, trigger runs
  • MCP registry — search_mcp_registry and mcp-registry-get. Installing a registry entry (mcp-registry-install) requires a platform-admin token, since it opens an outbound connection. A project's own servers are administered over REST, not through client tools — see Managing external servers

See apps/server/domain/mcp/README.md for the complete tools, resources, and prompts reference.

docs.title: Sending feedback about Memory
docs.text:
The built-in server exposes feedback-submit, and the same submission is available over REST as POST /api/feedback. Both accept the credential you already use and file the report as a GitHub issue, with your account, project and basic environment details attached automatically — you never need to paste a token or your email.

There is no strict template. Write what you were trying to do, what happened, and what you expected. If you can, add the steps that reproduce it and the exact error text; one or two sentences is fine when that is all you have.

{
  "message": "The entity search tool returns stale results for a few minutes after an update.",
  "category": "bug",
  "severity": "medium",
  "include_context": true
}

category (bug, feature, usability, docs, other) and severity (low, medium, high) are optional. include_context defaults to true; set it to false to send only your message and account identity. A caller is limited to a handful of submissions per hour, and an immediate retry of the same text returns the issue created by the first call instead of filing a duplicate.

A deployment that has no feedback tracker configured answers 503 and sends nothing anywhere — the endpoint is present, the destination is not.

docs.title: Sharing a scoped key with someone else
docs.text:
To hand an outside client — a teammate's agent, a partner, a demo — access to one project without giving it your own token, create a share: a named key bound to the exact tools you choose.

In the web UI: Settings → MCP Servers → Sharing → New share. Name the share, tick the tools it may call, and optionally enter one or more email addresses under Email the key. Each recipient receives the endpoint, the key, and ready-to-paste client configs; the sender is named in the email.

Presets. The create form offers a preset row that ticks a curated tool set in one click — it replaces the current selection, and you can adjust the ticks afterwards:

Preset What it grants Read-only (default) Search, graph reads, document and journal reads, schema reads, skill reads, and agent/run reads. No MCP tool in this set writes. Knowledge writer Read-only plus creating, editing, and deleting objects, relationships, documents, and journal notes. Schema & blueprints Graph reads, then schema read/write, schema migrations, and blueprints. Agent observer Agent, run, question, and session reads, plus search and graph reads. Documents Upload, list, retrieve, and delete documents, plus document classification, keyword search, and semantic search. Full access Every tool a share key can carry.

A share key is also an ordinary project API token, so the scopes behind the selected tools are honoured by the REST API as well as the MCP tools. Presets keep that set as narrow as the tools allow — the Documents preset, for example, grants document read/write and search but no knowledge or chat writes.

Presets never exceed what a share may grant: platform administration, project settings, credential minting, and agent execution/management are not shareable, so Full access is the ceiling rather than "admin". Each preset's tool count is resolved against your project's catalog when the page loads, so it always matches the tools the backend currently offers.

The same data is available to API clients: GET /api/projects/{projectId}/mcp/tools returns tools plus a templates array (id, label, description, tools, toolCount, and default on the preselected one). Creating a share still sends an explicit tools list — a template is a UI convenience, not a new request field. The list is required: a request with no tools (or an empty array) is rejected with HTTP 422. Shares created before the allowlist existed, and the legacy POST /api/projects/{projectId}/mcp/share endpoint, keep an unrestricted allowlist and remain read-only through their token scopes.

Copy an existing share. To start a new share from one that already works, open its ⋯ menu → Duplicate share. The create form opens pre-filled with that share's description and tool selection, under a free name (<name> (copy), or (copy 2) and so on when that name is taken); adjust anything and save. The copy is an ordinary new share with its own key — the source share, its key, and its invite recipients are untouched. Legacy shares can be copied this way too, which is how you move off one, even though they cannot be edited.

The key is shown to you exactly once, on the creation screen. If you also entered recipients, they have their own copy; otherwise copy it before closing the dialog.

To send the key to someone after the share exists, open the share's ⋯ menu → Invite by email. That emails the current key and the same ready-to-paste client configs, so anyone already using the share keeps working. Issue a new key in the same menu is the destructive alternative: the old key stops working immediately and its dialog offers the same optional email field. A share whose key was stored before the deployment enabled key encryption cannot be re-sent — the invite dialog says so and offers Issue a new key instead.

Who has the key, and what it did. A share records the addresses its key was emailed to: the Sharing list shows them (hover the chip for the full list) and marks a share read & write when its tools can modify the graph. The invite email says the same thing, so a recipient is never told a writable key is read-only. Choose View writes on a share to open the object browser filtered to the objects that share's key created or last updated. The filter follows the share's current key, so after Issue a new key it starts from that rotation instead of covering the retired key.

From the CLI: memory projects share-mcp --project my-project --email alice@example.com does the same through the legacy share endpoint and mints one key per recipient.

Sharing only ever narrows access: a share token carries just the scopes its selected tools require, so it cannot reach project administration or other projects.

docs.title: Brave Search integration
docs.text: The built-in server includes a brave_web_search tool backed by the Brave Search API. The API key can be set globally (via environment variable) or overridden per-org or per-project — see Built-in tool configuration below.

docs.title: Built-in tool configuration
docs.text:
Built-in tools can be enabled/disabled and configured at three levels. The most specific level wins:

project setting  →  org default  →  global env var

If a project has no explicit setting, it inherits from the org default. If neither is set, the global environment variable is used.

docs.title: Available built-in tools
docs.text: Tool Env var (global fallback) Config field brave_web_search BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY api_key

docs.title: Project-level configuration
docs.text:
List the builtin server and its tools for your project:

# 1. Find the builtin server ID (auto-created on first list)
curl "https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers?projectId=<projectId>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
# → find the entry with "type": "builtin"

# 2. List its tools (includes inheritedFrom field)
curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/<builtinServerId>/tools \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Each tool in the response includes an inheritedFrom field: "project", "org", or "global", indicating where the current effective setting comes from.

Enable/disable a built-in tool at project level:

curl -X PATCH "https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/<builtinServerId>/tools/<toolId>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": false}'

Set a per-project API key for brave_web_search:

curl -X PATCH "https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/<builtinServerId>/tools/<toolId>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "config": { "api_key": "BSA..." }
  }'

Once set, this project's agent runs use this API key instead of the global BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY.

docs.title: Org-level defaults
docs.text:
Org defaults apply to all projects in the org that have no project-level override.

List current org defaults:

curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/orgs/<orgId>/tool-settings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Set an org default (enable + API key):

curl -X PUT "https://api.example.com/api/admin/orgs/<orgId>/tool-settings/brave_web_search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "config": { "api_key": "BSA..." }
  }'

Disable brave_web_search for all projects in the org by default:

curl -X PUT "https://api.example.com/api/admin/orgs/<orgId>/tool-settings/brave_web_search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": false}'

Remove an org default (projects fall back to the global env var):

curl -X DELETE "https://api.example.com/api/admin/orgs/<orgId>/tool-settings/brave_web_search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Inheritance example
docs.text:
Suppose you want brave_web_search enabled for most projects but one project should use a different API key:

Global env: BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY=BSA-global-key

Org default: enabled=true, api_key=BSA-org-key      ← applies to all projects by default
  Project A: (no override)                          → uses org key (inheritedFrom: "org")
  Project B: api_key=BSA-project-b-key             → uses project B key (inheritedFrom: "project")
  Project C: enabled=false                          → tool disabled for this project

docs.title: UI
docs.text:
The MCP Integration settings page (Project Settings → Integrations → MCP Integration) has a Built-in Tools section where you can toggle tools and set config fields for the current project.

The Tool Defaults page (Project Settings → Organization → Tool Defaults) lets org admins set org-wide defaults for all built-in tools.

docs.title: External MCP server registry
docs.text: Each project can register external MCP servers. These servers are proxied on demand and their tool catalogs are mirrored locally so agents can discover tools without connecting to every server on each request.

docs.title: Server types
docs.text: Type type value Connection Built-in (Memory) builtin Internal; not configurable Subprocess (local) stdio Launches a command with arguments Server-Sent Events sse Long-lived HTTP SSE connection Plain HTTP http Per-request HTTP

docs.title: List registered servers
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Register a stdio server
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "filesystem",
    "type": "stdio",
    "command": "npx",
    "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/tmp/workspace"],
    "env": {},
    "enabled": true
  }'

docs.title: Register an SSE server
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-sse-server",
    "type": "sse",
    "url": "https://my-mcp-server.example.com/sse",
    "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <server-token>" },
    "enabled": true
  }'

docs.title: Register an HTTP server
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-http-server",
    "type": "http",
    "url": "https://my-mcp-server.example.com/mcp",
    "headers": {},
    "enabled": true
  }'

docs.title: Import a Claude MCP config
docs.text:
Memory can import the mcpServers format used by Claude Desktop (claude_desktop_config.json), Claude Code (.mcp.json / ~/.claude.json), and claude mcp add-json. Each valid entry is created; malformed entries and name conflicts are reported without aborting the rest.

# From a file
memory agents mcp-servers import --from-claude ~/.claude.json --device laptop-connector

# From stdin
cat claude_desktop_config.json | memory agents mcp-servers import --from-claude -

# Preview the plan without writing
memory agents mcp-servers import --from-claude ./.mcp.json --device laptop-connector --dry-run

Delivery is chosen per entry by default (--target auto):

Entry Lands as http / sse (remote) a server-target registry row, connected outbound by the Memory host stdio (local command) a device-target registry row, pushed to the connector named by --device

--target server forces every entry onto the Memory host; --target device forces every entry onto the connector. A stdio entry without a device is a broadcast, which only project admins may create. Existing names are skipped unless --overwrite is passed. ${VAR} placeholders in env/headers values are stored literally — Memory does not expand them.

The same import is available in the web UI (Settings → MCP Servers → Add server → Import from Claude) and over the REST API:

curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/import \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "config": {"mcpServers": {"github": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "pkg"]}}},
    "target": "auto",
    "targetInstanceId": "laptop-connector",
    "overwrite": false,
    "dryRun": false
  }'

The response lists created, updated, skipped, and failed entries.

Local stdio entries are better imported by the connector itself, which runs them on the machine that owns the command. In the macOS connector app open Hosted MCP Servers → Import from Claude…, or on a Linux connector run:

memory-connector mcp import --from-claude ~/.claude.json --dry-run
memory-connector mcp import --from-claude ~/.claude.json --overwrite

The connector import refuses while the connector is running (it would race the config file); use the app or its loopback management API for a live connector. An overwrite keeps the existing server's enabled state and disabled_tools.

docs.title: Inspect a server (preview tools without saving)
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/<serverId>/inspect \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Returns the tool list from the live server without persisting anything.

docs.title: Sync tool catalog
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/<serverId>/sync \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Connects to the server, calls tools/list, and upserts results into the local tool catalog. Safe to call repeatedly (idempotent).

docs.title: List synced tools
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/<serverId>/tools \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Enable / disable a tool
docs.text:
curl -X PATCH https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/<serverId>/tools/<toolId> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": false}'

Disabled tools are filtered from the agent context.

docs.title: Update a server
docs.text:
curl -X PATCH https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/<serverId> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": false}'

docs.title: Delete a server
docs.text:
curl -X DELETE https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-servers/<serverId> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Official MCP registry
docs.text: Browse and install servers from the official MCP registry at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io.

docs.title: Search the registry
docs.text:
curl "https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-registry/search?q=github" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Get details for a registry server
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-registry/servers/github \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Install from the registry
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/mcp-registry/install \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "serverName": "github",
    "config": {
      "env": { "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "ghp_..." }
    }
  }'

This creates a new MCPServer record for your project and immediately runs a sync to populate the tool catalog.

docs.title: Server entity reference
docs.text:
MCPServer — table kb.mcp_servers

Field Type Description id UUID Primary key projectId UUID Owning project name string Display name enabled bool Disabled servers are not proxied type string stdio | sse | http | builtin command string Executable path (stdio only) args string[] Arguments (stdio only) env object Environment variables (stdio only) url string Server URL (sse/http only) headers object HTTP headers (sse/http only) createdAt timestamp updatedAt timestamp

MCPServerTool — table kb.mcp_server_tools

Field Type Description id UUID Primary key serverId UUID FK → mcp_servers toolName string As reported by the server description string Tool description inputSchema object JSON Schema for tool inputs enabled bool Disabled tools are hidden from agents createdAt timestamp

docs.title: Hosted MCP servers (workspace)
docs.text: For persistent, containerized MCP servers managed by the workspace system, contact your platform administrator.

docs.title: Provider Setup
docs.text: Memory uses LLM providers for text generation (chat, agents) and embedding (vector search). Credentials are configured at the org level as a default, and can be overridden at the project level when a project needs a different model or billing account.

docs.title: Supported providers
docs.text: Provider provider value Auth method Google AI (Gemini API) google-ai API key Google Cloud Vertex AI vertex-ai Service account JSON

docs.title: Credential security
docs.text: Credentials are AES-GCM encrypted at rest and never returned by any API response. The configured flag in responses indicates whether a credential is stored without revealing the value.

docs.title: Org-level configuration
docs.text: Org-level credentials are the default fallback for all projects in the org.

docs.title: Configure Google AI (Gemini API)
docs.text:
curl -X PUT https://api.example.com/api/v1/organizations/<orgId>/providers/google-ai \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "apiKey": "AIza...",
    "generativeModel": "gemini-2.0-flash",
    "embeddingModel": "text-embedding-004"
  }'

docs.title: Configure Vertex AI
docs.text:
curl -X PUT https://api.example.com/api/v1/organizations/<orgId>/providers/vertex-ai \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "serviceAccountJson": "{\"type\":\"service_account\", ...}",
    "gcpProject": "my-gcp-project",
    "location": "us-central1",
    "generativeModel": "gemini-2.0-flash",
    "embeddingModel": "text-embedding-004"
  }'

docs.title: Check configuration status
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/v1/organizations/<orgId>/providers/google-ai \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

{
  "provider": "google-ai",
  "configured": true,
  "generativeModel": "gemini-2.0-flash",
  "embeddingModel": "text-embedding-004",
  "updatedAt": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z"
}

docs.title: List all configured providers
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/v1/organizations/<orgId>/providers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Remove a provider
docs.text:
curl -X DELETE https://api.example.com/api/v1/organizations/<orgId>/providers/google-ai \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Project-level overrides
docs.text:
A project-level config overrides the org default for that project only. Useful when:

  • A project needs a different billing account
  • A project requires a different model (e.g. a larger context model for long documents)
  • You are running A/B tests across projects
curl -X PUT https://api.example.com/api/v1/projects/<projectId>/providers/google-ai \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "apiKey": "AIza...",
    "generativeModel": "gemini-2.5-pro",
    "embeddingModel": "text-embedding-004"
  }'

The resolution order is: project config → org config → error.

docs.title: Testing a provider
docs.text:
Before relying on a provider for production workloads, test the credentials:

curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/providers/google-ai/test \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"apiKey": "AIza..."}'

Returns 200 OK with a {"success": true} body on success, or an error message on failure.

docs.title: Listing available models
docs.text:
Retrieve the model catalog for a provider:

curl "https://api.example.com/api/v1/providers/google-ai/models?type=generative" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

The type query parameter accepts generative or embedding.

docs.title: PUT /api/v1/organizations/:orgId/providers/:provider
docs.text: Field Type Required Description apiKey string Google AI only Gemini API key serviceAccountJson string Vertex AI only Full service account JSON as a string gcpProject string Vertex AI only GCP project ID location string Vertex AI only Region, e.g. us-central1 generativeModel string No Override default generative model name embeddingModel string No Override default embedding model name

docs.title: Usage tracking
docs.text: Every LLM call is recorded asynchronously. Events are buffered and bulk-inserted every 5 seconds (or at 100 events, whichever comes first).

docs.title: View org usage
docs.text:
curl "https://api.example.com/api/v1/organizations/<orgId>/usage?since=2026-03-01" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: View project usage
docs.text:
curl "https://api.example.com/api/v1/projects/<projectId>/usage" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Usage event fields
docs.text:
Field Description provider google-ai or vertex-ai model Model name operation generate or embed textInputTokens Text tokens sent to the model imageInputTokens Image tokens (multimodal) outputTokens Tokens in the response estimatedCostUsd Estimated cost in USD createdAt Timestamp

Cost estimates use org-configured custom rates when available, falling back to global retail rates per 1M tokens.

docs.title: Model name examples
docs.text: Use case Model General generation (fast) gemini-2.0-flash Extended context / reasoning gemini-2.5-pro Embeddings text-embedding-004

docs.title: Sandboxes
docs.text: Sandboxes are isolated compute environments where AI agents execute code. They support multiple sandbox technologies and can be used for both one-off agent runs (ephemeral) and long-running development sessions (persistent).

docs.title: Host requirements (self-hosted)
docs.text: Running sandboxes on your own host requires Docker Engine 29.5.1 or newer. Sandbox operations execute against the host's dockerd through the mounted /var/run/docker.sock, so earlier engines remain exposed to the docker cp / archive advisories GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r, GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5 and GHSA-rg2x-37c3-w2rh, and to GHSA-pxq6-2prw-chj9 (fixed from 29.3.1). The Go dependency pin cannot remediate daemon-side code — an Engine upgrade is the only fix — and an out-of-date daemon is the real attack surface when sandboxes run untrusted code. The installation requirements in deploy/self-hosted/INSTALL.md are authoritative.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Concept Description Sandbox An isolated container with optional git checkout Provider The underlying sandbox technology Lifecycle ephemeral (auto-cleaned) or persistent (manually managed) Container type agent_sandbox (for code execution) or mcp_server (for hosted MCP) Hosted MCP server A persistent sandbox running an MCP server container

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: Provider provider value Technology Firecracker firecracker Firecracker microVMs — highest isolation E2B e2b E2B cloud sandboxes gVisor gvisor gVisor container runtime

docs.title: Sandbox lifecycle
docs.text:
creating → ready → (stopping → stopped)
                ↘ error
Status Description creating Sandbox is being provisioned ready Sandbox is running and accepting tool calls stopping Graceful shutdown in progress stopped Sandbox is stopped (can be resumed) error Provisioning or runtime error

docs.title: List sandboxes
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: List available providers
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/providers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Create a sandbox
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "firecracker",
    "lifecycle": "ephemeral",
    "repositoryUrl": "https://github.com/my-org/my-repo",
    "branch": "main",
    "resourceLimits": {
      "cpu": 2,
      "memoryMb": 2048,
      "diskGb": 10
    },
    "metadata": {
      "purpose": "code-review"
    }
  }'

docs.title: Create from snapshot
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/from-snapshot \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "snapshotId": "<snapshot-id>",
    "provider": "firecracker"
  }'

docs.title: Stop a sandbox
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/<id>/stop \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Resume a stopped sandbox
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/<id>/resume \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Take a snapshot
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/<id>/snapshot \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Returns {"snapshotId": "..."}. Use with from-snapshot to create pre-warmed sandboxes.

docs.title: Delete a sandbox
docs.text:
curl -X DELETE https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/<id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Tool execution
docs.text: Once a sandbox is ready, you can execute tools inside it. All tool calls are recorded in the audit log.

docs.title: Bash
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/<id>/bash \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "command": "npm test",
    "timeout": 60000,
    "workdir": "/sandbox"
  }'

Response: { "stdout": "...", "stderr": "...", "exitCode": 0, "timedOut": false }

docs.title: Read a file
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/<id>/read \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

docs.title: Glob

curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/<id>/glob \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \

Response: { "files": ["/sandbox/src/main.go", ...] }

curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/agent/sandboxes/<id>/grep \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \

Response: { "matches": [{ "file": "...", "line": 42, "content": "// TODO: fix this" }] }

docs.title: Tool audit log
docs.text:
Every tool call is recorded in kb.sandbox_audit_log:

Field Description sandboxId The sandbox where the tool ran agentSessionId The agent session that triggered the call toolName bash, read, write, edit, glob, grep, or git requestPayloadHash SHA-256 hash of the request body responseStatus HTTP status of the tool response durationMs Execution time in milliseconds

docs.title: Hosted MCP servers
docs.text: You can run persistent MCP server containers inside the sandbox system. These are separate from the project MCP registry — they are containerized processes managed by the sandbox orchestrator.

docs.title: List hosted servers
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/v1/mcp/hosted \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Register a hosted server
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/mcp/hosted \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-server",
    "imageRef": "my-registry.example.com/my-mcp-server:latest",
    "command": ["node", "server.js"],
    "env": { "NODE_ENV": "production" },
    "mcpConfig": { "tools": ["my_tool"] }
  }'

docs.title: Call a hosted server
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/mcp/hosted/<id>/call \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": { "name": "my_tool", "arguments": {} }
  }'

docs.title: Restart a hosted server
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/mcp/hosted/<id>/restart \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Delete a hosted server
docs.text:
curl -X DELETE https://api.example.com/api/v1/mcp/hosted/<id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Sandbox images
docs.text: Sandbox images are the base Docker images used when creating sandboxes. Global images are available to all projects; project-scoped images are private.

docs.title: List images
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/admin/sandbox-images \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Register a custom image
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/admin/sandbox-images \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "node-18-sandbox",
    "dockerRef": "my-registry.example.com/node-18-sandbox:latest",
    "provider": "gvisor",
    "type": "custom"
  }'

Image status transitions: pending → pulling → ready (or error on failure).

docs.title: Delete an image
docs.text:
curl -X DELETE https://api.example.com/api/admin/sandbox-images/<id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Background Scheduler
docs.text: The scheduler runs maintenance tasks on a fixed cron schedule. It has no HTTP endpoints — it is an internal subsystem that runs automatically when the server starts.

docs.title: Scheduled tasks
docs.text:
Task Schedule Description RevisionCountRefreshTask Every 15 minutes Refreshes cached revision counts on graph nodes to avoid expensive COUNT queries at read time TagCleanupTask Every 30 minutes Removes orphaned tags (tags with no associated objects) CacheCleanupTask Every hour Evicts stale entries from in-memory and DB-backed caches StaleJobCleanupTask Every 10 minutes Marks jobs that have been stuck in processing state beyond their timeout as failed, recovering from worker crashes

All tasks run with a 30-minute hard timeout. If a task exceeds this limit it is cancelled and the error is logged; the next scheduled run will attempt it again automatically.

docs.title: Cron expression format
docs.text:
The scheduler uses robfig/cron with seconds precision (6-field expressions):

┌─────── second (0–59)
│ ┌───── minute (0–59)
│ │ ┌─── hour (0–23)
│ │ │ ┌─ day of month (1–31)
│ │ │ │ ┌ month (1–12)
│ │ │ │ │ ┌ day of week (0–6, Sunday=0)
│ │ │ │ │ │
* * * * * *

Examples:

Expression Runs 0 */15 * * * * Every 15 minutes 0 */30 * * * * Every 30 minutes 0 0 * * * * Every hour, on the hour 0 */10 * * * * Every 10 minutes

docs.title: Stale job detection
docs.text:
The StaleJobCleanupTask is particularly important for reliability. If a worker process crashes while a job is in processing state, the job would otherwise remain stuck indefinitely. This task detects jobs that have exceeded their expected processing time and marks them as failed, making them eligible for retry.

The timeout threshold per job type:

Job type Timeout threshold Document parsing 30 minutes Object extraction 60 minutes Chunk embedding 15 minutes Graph embedding 15 minutes Datasource sync 60 minutes

docs.title: Observability
docs.text:
Scheduler task runs are logged at the INFO level:

INFO  scheduler: task started name=RevisionCountRefreshTask
INFO  scheduler: task completed name=RevisionCountRefreshTask duration=1.2s
WARN  scheduler: task exceeded timeout name=TagCleanupTask duration=30m0s
ERROR scheduler: task failed name=StaleJobCleanupTask error="context canceled"

The scheduler itself starts and stops gracefully with the server (via fx lifecycle hooks). On shutdown, the scheduler waits for any in-progress task to complete or be cancelled before the process exits.

docs.title: Schema Registry
docs.text: The schema registry defines the schema of objects that can live in your project's knowledge graph. Every object has a type name, and the registry stores the JSON Schema, display config, and extraction hints for each type.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Concept Description Type A named schema: what properties an object can have and how it behaves Source Where the type came from: schema, custom, or discovered Embedding policy Controls whether and how objects of this type are embedded for vector search

docs.title: Type sources
docs.text: Source Description schema Installed from a schema custom Created directly by a developer discovered Proposed automatically by the extraction pipeline

docs.title: List types
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/schema-registry/projects/<projectId> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Get a specific type
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/schema-registry/projects/<projectId>/types/Person \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

docs.title: Get type version history
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/schema-registry/projects/<projectId>/types/Person/versions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Returns the persisted version history for a type, newest first. Each schema_version has one snapshot, and active is true on the version matching the current registry row. Existing types are backfilled at their current version, and a DB trigger keeps the history current automatically. Returns 404 if the type does not exist.

{
  "project_id": "<projectId>",
  "type_name": "Person",
  "current_version": 3,
  "versions": [
    {
      "registry_id": "<uuid>",
      "schema_version": 3,
      "json_schema": { "...": "..." },
      "ui_config": { "...": "..." },
      "extraction_config": { "...": "..." },
      "enabled": true,
      "description": "A person",
      "namespace": null,
      "created_by": "<uuid>",
      "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "active": true
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Get type stats
docs.text:
curl https://api.example.com/api/schema-registry/projects/<projectId>/stats \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Returns counts of total / enabled / by-source types.

docs.title: Create a custom type
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/schema-registry/projects/<projectId>/types \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "typeName": "Company",
    "description": "A business entity",
    "jsonSchema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "name":        { "type": "string" },
        "industry":    { "type": "string" },
        "founded":     { "type": "integer" },
        "headquarters":{ "type": "string" }
      },
      "required": ["name"]
    },
    "uiConfig": {
      "icon": "building",
      "color": "#4f46e5",
      "displayProperty": "name"
    },
    "extractionConfig": {
      "extractRelationships": true,
      "confidenceThreshold": 0.7
    },
    "enabled": true
  }'

docs.title: Update a type
docs.text:
curl -X PUT https://api.example.com/api/schema-registry/projects/<projectId>/types/Company \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "description": "A business entity (updated)",
    "enabled": true
  }'

docs.title: Delete a type
docs.text:
curl -X DELETE https://api.example.com/api/schema-registry/projects/<projectId>/types/Company \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Cascade impact

Deleting a type does not delete existing graph objects of that type. Those objects remain but will no longer be validated against the schema or included in extractions.
