A Gmail source ingests one document per thread: a Markdown document with a header (subject, participants, latest message, labels) and one section per message, oldest first. Message bodies use the plain-text part, falling back to a conversion of the HTML part; attachments are counted (_N attachment(s) omitted._) but never downloaded.

Field Meaning Query (query) Gmail search expression selecting which threads sync. Default in:inbox. Examples: label:work, from:alice@example.com, -label:spam, has:attachment. Label ids (label_ids) Optional label ids; a thread must carry every listed label. List them from the source's resources (GET /api/data-source-integrations/{id}/resources) or the provider catalog (POST /api/data-source-integrations/resources). When labels are set and no query is given, the source syncs everything carrying those labels instead of the inbox. Since (since) Optional YYYY-MM-DD. Threads dated before it are never synced. The date is absolute, so the window only grows: a source never drops previously synced threads just because time passed. Gmail's after: filter is day-granular in the mailbox's own timezone, so a thread dated on the boundary day may be included or excluded by a few hours. Max threads (max_threads) Ceiling for one pass. Default 10000, maximum 50000. Every sync lists the newest matching threads; when the query matches more than the ceiling, older threads are backfilled a calendar window at a time on later syncs (see below), so a large mailbox is eventually covered instead of only ever contributing its newest slice.

A capped listing is not a dead end. The sync that hits the ceiling starts walking older windows (30 days at a time, narrowing when a window is larger than one sync may ingest) and stores a coverage watermark in the source's cursor. Each following sync continues from that watermark — head first, so new mail still arrives immediately — until the walk reaches the since floor (or, without a since, Gmail's earliest possible date). Because every window overlaps the next by a day, re-listing a thread costs only a skipped revision, never a gap — the one exception is a day holding more matching threads than max_threads, which is capped exactly as a capped listing always was. A sync whose threads fail to fetch leaves the watermark where it was, so that window is re-listed and the failures retried. That retry is bounded per thread: a thread that fails to fetch or apply on three consecutive syncs is abandoned so one broken message cannot freeze the backfill forever, and the sync that moves past it records the abandoned thread ids in its error detail and leaves the reason on the source's last error. Different threads each failing once never exhaust that budget. Because a Gmail source never deletes, a window you later tightened keeps what it already ingested.

Windows are calendar ranges, not listing pages, so a modified old thread is picked up when its window is next re-listed rather than on the very next sync.

Change detection uses Gmail's per-thread history id: an unchanged thread is skipped without downloading its body, so re-syncing a large mailbox is cheap. A thread that gains a message or changes labels is re-read, and produces a new document version only when its text actually changed. Gmail bills threads.list at 10 units and threads.get at 120 units (the connector requests full threads) against 6,000 units per minute per user, so a rate-limited call is retried with exponential backoff — honouring Retry-After — instead of failing the thread until the next scheduled sync.

Gmail scope and Google verification

The connector requests gmail.readonly, a Google restricted scope. A Google Cloud project whose consent screen is Internal (Workspace-only) can use it without review; an External app needs Google verification and a CASA assessment before non-test users can consent. A consent screen left in Testing also expires every Google grant after 7 days, Drive included — see Create the app in the vendor console. Enable the Gmail API, add the scope, and register the callback https://<api-host>/api/data-source-integrations/oauth/gmail/callback — see Create the app in the vendor console.

Deleted mail is not detected in this version

A Gmail sync is a filtered view of a live mailbox: a thread absent from it may have been archived, relabelled, or moved out of the query rather than deleted. Gmail sources therefore never mark documents deleted-from-source. Deletion detection via the mailbox history is a follow-up.

docs.title: Reconnecting a source
docs.text:
An OAuth grant can stop working long before you want to delete the source: the user revokes the app in their Google or GitHub account, the refresh token expires, or the provider rotates it away. The sync then fails with the provider's error, and the source's Credentials card offers Reconnect.

A failure of this kind parks the source: its status becomes Needs reconnect and scheduled syncs stop until it is reconnected. That is deliberate. Re-sending a grant the provider has already rejected cannot succeed, so a parked source is not retried — before this it kept producing a failed sync every minute while the connections table still called it active. The error stays on the source and in its sync history, and no documents are removed. A transient failure (a 5xx, a timeout, a rate limit) never parks a source; it stays active and retries on its normal cadence.

If you believe the grant is fine — the provider had an outage, or the failure was misclassified — you can retry without a new consent by setting enabled: true on the source (PATCH /api/data-source-integrations/{id}; there is no on/off control for a data source in the UI yet). That returns it to active and clears the recorded failure, so the API stops reporting the old message (errorMessage) on a source that is syncing again; the failed run stays in the sync history. A scheduled source syncs on its next sweep, and a manual one syncs when you press Sync now. A grant that really is dead parks the source again.

Consent runs again for the same source. The stored grant is replaced in place, so the source keeps its id, name, sync targets, cursor and sync history — the next sync resumes instead of re-importing everything into a second source. The connected account and the granted scope strategy are refreshed from the new consent, and the recorded error clears.

The action follows the provider's advertised auth methods. A web source has no OAuth method and shows none. A GitHub source always shows it, including one connected with a personal access token — reconnecting replaces that token with an OAuth grant for the same source, so it needs the GitHub OAuth app to be configured.

Reconnect is not a new source

Reconnecting never creates a second source. If you see a duplicate after a provider authorization, it came from the connect flow, not from Reconnect.

Over the API, name the source on the authorize request and the callback updates that source. The endpoint takes a JSON body, so send the content type with it:

curl -X GET "$MEMORY_API_URL/api/data-source-integrations/providers/google_drive/oauth/authorize" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"reconnectSourceId": "<source id>"}'

The response is the provider's authorize URL; without a readable body the request is treated as a plain connect and creates a new source.

docs.title: Connect GitHub with a personal access token
docs.text:
GitHub can be connected either with OAuth or with a personal access token. The token path uses a saved credential:

  1. Open Project Settings → Credentials and choose Add credential: pick GitHub, give the credential a name, and paste the token. (You can also do this inline from the connect form.)
  2. On Data Sources → New data source, pick GitHub and choose Use a personal access token.
  3. Select the saved credential. The list shows how many sources already use each one, so reusing an existing token is an informed choice.
  4. Fill in the repository scope below and press Connect.

The token is stored encrypted and write-only — it is never shown again. One saved credential can back several GitHub sources; editing it updates all of them.

Field How to fill it Repository Press Load repositories to pick from the repositories the token can see (private ones included), or type owner/name directly. Ref Once a repository is set, press Load branches and tags to pick a branch or tag, or type any ref. An empty ref syncs the repository's default branch. Commit SHAs are valid refs but are not listed. Paths / Extensions Optional filters limiting which files sync.

Press Test connection to validate the token and repository before saving.

The suggestion lists are best-effort. If a list cannot be loaded — an expired token, a rate limit, a fine-grained token without repository-list permission — the field shows an inline message and keeps the value you typed, so you can still connect. Picking from a list is never required: typing owner/name and a ref always works, including for GitHub Enterprise Server (whose API endpoint is configured for the whole deployment, not per source).

docs.title: GitHub token scopes
docs.text:
• Classic token: the repo scope to read private repositories and their contents (public_repo is enough for public repositories).
  • Fine-grained token: Repository metadata: Read to list the repositories the token can see, and Contents: Read on the target repository to list branches and tags and sync its files.

Reading branches and tags needs no permission beyond contents access.

docs.title: Trale (meeting intelligence)
docs.text:
Trale imports meeting transcripts and their AI-generated summaries. It connects over OAuth, but unlike Google Drive and GitHub it registers its own OAuth client at connect time using dynamic client registration (RFC 7591). There is no app to create in a vendor console and no client id/secret to enter, so the credentials pages simply do not list Trale — connect it directly from Data Sources.

Field Meaning Tags Required. The Trale tag slugs to import, for example standup. Pick from the suggestions the provider returns, or type them. Name pattern Optional regex matched against a meeting's title; only matching meetings are imported. Include transcript When enabled, the full transcript is imported as part of the document. Off (the default) imports the summary and structured summary only. Backfill days How far back to look for past meetings (default 90).

Only completed meetings are imported. The document's identity is derived from the meeting's status, participant count, tags, and summary, so a meeting that is later re-summarized updates in place rather than duplicating.

Operational caveats:

  • No modification timestamp. Trale does not expose one, so change detection rests on the composite identity above: a meeting whose status, participant count, tags and summary are unchanged is not fetched again. That keeps repeat syncs cheap, but an edit that only touches the transcript is not picked up until another part of that identity changes.
  • Plan or access lapses surface as errors. If the Trale plan lapses or the connected account loses access, the sync fails with a connection error rather than reporting an empty success.
  • Per-user visibility. Trale returns the meetings the authorizing account can see, so a data source imports exactly that account's meeting scope.
  • 25 meetings per call. Enumeration pages through meetings 25 at a time; a large backfill takes several calls and nothing is silently truncated.
  • Token rotation is persisted. The authorization server rotates the refresh token on every use, and the source stores the rotated token, so routine rotation never interrupts syncing. A refresh fails only when the grant itself is revoked or has expired; the source then stops with an actionable error, and the source's detail page offers Reconnect to repair the grant in place.
  • A park that survives a reconnect is usually a client problem, not a grant problem. Trale's authorization server reports a dead grant and a misconfigured client registration with the same error code (invalid_credentials), so the message cannot tell them apart. If the source parks again after a successful reconnect, stop reconnecting — the OAuth client registration is wrong or was deleted, and no number of reconnects will fix it, so an administrator has to correct the client configuration. A sync that was already running when you reconnected cannot cause it: it keeps failing against the grant it started with, but it records that failure without parking the source, because the grant you just replaced is not the one the source reads any more.

docs.title: Web (website crawl)
docs.text:
The web provider crawls a website starting from one or more URLs and imports each page as a Markdown document. It connects with config only — no credentials are collected or stored.

Field Meaning Start URLs (start_urls) Required. One or more absolute http(s) URLs to start from (up to 50). The crawl stays on the same origin as each start URL. Include globs (include_globs) Optional URL path globs to keep, for example /docs/**. Empty keeps every in-scope page. Exclude globs (exclude_globs) Optional URL path globs to skip, for example /admin/**. Max pages (max_pages) Maximum pages to crawl. Default and ceiling is 200. Max depth (max_depth) Maximum link depth to follow. Default 3; 0 ingests only the start URLs (no link following).
  • Static HTML only. Each page is fetched and converted to Markdown. The crawler does not execute JavaScript, so sites that render their content client-side will ingest poorly.
  • robots.txt is honored. The crawler respects the site's robots.txt and identifies itself with an EmergentMemoryBot/1.0 user agent.
  • Caps. A single crawl is capped at 200 pages, 5 MiB per page, and 50 MiB in total.
  • Politeness. The crawler waits at least 1 second between requests to the same host.
  • Sync cadence. Sources sync every 60 minutes by default; the fastest allowed interval is 15 minutes.
  • Removals are proof-based. A page returning 404/410 is re-checked once before it is marked deleted_from_source (soft-deleted) — a transient failure never deletes a page.

docs.title: Setting Up a Data Source
docs.text:
Admin UIAPI

Go to Data Sources → New data source and select your provider.

POST /api/data-source-integrations
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Team inbox",
  "providerType": "gmail",
  "sourceType": "email",
  "syncMode": "scheduled",
  "syncIntervalMinutes": 60,
  "config": { "query": "in:inbox -label:spam" }
}

After creation you will be redirected (or given a URL) to complete the OAuth flow for providers that require it.

docs.title: Test the connection before saving
docs.text:
POST /api/data-source-integrations/test-config
{
  "providerType": "web",
  "config": {
    "start_urls": ["https://docs.example.com/"]
  }
}

A saved source can be tested without resending config:

POST /api/data-source-integrations/{id}/test-connection

docs.title: Data source fields
Choosing Sync Targets Through the API
docs.text:
The folder-picker modal saves through the same endpoint an API client can call. Submit only folder ids; the server resolves each folder's name and shared-drive id from Drive and merges the result into the source config while preserving its other keys:

PUT /api/data-source-integrations/{id}/sync-targets
Content-Type: application/json

{ "folderIds": ["1AbC…", "1XyZ…"] }

An empty list, an inaccessible folder, or more than 50 ids is rejected. The response is the updated integration. The picker itself mints a short-lived access token from the source's own stored refresh token via GET /api/data-source-integrations/{id}/picker-session (UI-only; the token is never logged or cached).

docs.title: Triggering a Sync
docs.text:
Manually trigger a sync at any time:

POST /api/data-source-integrations/{id}/sync

docs.title: Monitoring Sync Jobs
docs.text:
GET /api/data-source-integrations/{id}/sync-jobs?limit=50&offset=0  # one page, newest first
GET /api/data-source-integrations/{id}/sync-jobs/latest             # most recent
GET /api/data-source-integrations/{id}/sync-jobs/{jobId}            # specific job

The listing is paged. limit defaults to 50 and is capped at 200; offset skips that many jobs so older history can be fetched page by page. The response's items is the requested page and total is the source's full job count (not the page length). Pass status to filter the listing.

docs.title: Sync job fields
docs.text: Field Description status pending · running · completed · failed · cancelled totalItems Total items discovered processedItems Items processed so far successfulItems Items imported successfully failedItems Items that failed to import skippedItems Items skipped (already up to date) currentPhase Current processing phase label statusMessage Human-readable progress description

docs.title: Cancelling a Sync
docs.text: POST /api/data-source-integrations/{id}/sync-jobs/{jobId}/cancel

docs.title: Schema Discovery
docs.text:
For structured data sources (e.g. databases, APIs), you can run a discovery job to infer object types from the source schema:

POST /api/discovery-jobs/projects/{projectId}/start
{
  "integrationId": "<data-source-id>"
}

Monitor the discovery job:

GET /api/discovery-jobs/{jobId}

Finalize (apply discovered types to the type registry):

POST /api/discovery-jobs/{jobId}/finalize

docs.title: Listing Data Sources
docs.text:
GET /api/data-source-integrations
GET /api/data-source-integrations/source-types        # available source types
GET /api/data-source-integrations/providers           # available provider configs
GET /api/data-source-integrations/providers/{type}/schema  # config schema for a provider

docs.title: Updating and Deleting
docs.text:
PATCH  /api/data-source-integrations/{id}    # update name, syncMode, etc.
DELETE /api/data-source-integrations/{id}    # remove integration

enabled is the pause/resume switch, and the only way to retry a parked source without reconnecting:

PATCH /api/data-source-integrations/{id}
Content-Type: application/json

{ "enabled": true }

Note

Deleting a data source does not delete the documents already imported from it. Those remain in the project.

docs.title: Documents
docs.text: Documents are files, URLs, or plain text that you upload into a project. The platform automatically chunks and indexes them so their content becomes searchable and extractable into the knowledge graph.

docs.title: Supported sources
docs.text: Source type Description File upload PDF, Word, Markdown, plain text, and other formats URL Web pages fetched and converted to text Text Raw text content submitted directly via API Data source sync Documents imported automatically from connected integrations (see Data Sources)

docs.title: Uploading a Document
docs.text:
CLIAPI (file)API (URL) 
memory documents upload ./report.pdf --project my-project
memory documents upload https://example.com/spec.html --project my-project

POST /api/documents/upload
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

file=@report.pdf

POST /api/documents
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "sourceUrl": "https://example.com/spec.html",
  "sourceType": "url"
}

After upload the document enters a conversion pipeline: the file is parsed, split into chunks, and each chunk is embedded for semantic search.

docs.title: Document fields
docs.text: Field Description filename Original file name sourceUrl URL if the document came from a web source mimeType Detected MIME type fileSizeBytes File size conversionStatus pending · processing · completed · failed chunks Number of text chunks created embeddedChunks Number of chunks with embeddings (ready for semantic search) totalChars Total character count across all chunks extractionStatus Status of AI entity extraction (if auto-extraction is enabled) processingStatus One derived state for the whole pipeline (see Document status) version 1 for an original, N for the Nth revision of a data-source document

docs.title: Listing Documents
docs.text:
CLIAPI 
memory documents list --project my-project

GET /api/documents?projectId={id}&limit=50

The listing is cursor-paginated and returns the page's documents, the total number of documents matching the filters, a per-status breakdown, and the cursor of the next page:

{
  "documents": [ { "id": "doc_1", "filename": "report.pdf", "processingStatus": "completed", "version": 1 } ],
  "total": 137,
  "statusCounts": { "all": 137, "processing": 4, "ready": 18, "extracted": 112, "failed": 3 },
  "next_cursor": "eyJzb3J0IjoiY3JlYXRlZCIs..."
}

docs.title: Query parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Values Description limit 1–500 (default 100) Page size cursor opaque string Next-page cursor from the previous response. Must be used with the same sort status processing · ready · extracted · failed One status bucket (omit for all) sourceType upload, drive, repo, email, meeting, web Only documents from that source kind; upload means files uploaded directly sourceId a connected data source id, or none Only documents from that data source; none means files uploaded directly with no data source q text (≤ 200 characters) Case-insensitive match over the file name and the source URL; % and _ are matched literally. Document content is not searched — use Search for that sort created (default) · updated Timestamp to order by order desc (default) · asc Direction

Pagination is keyset-based, so pages stay stable while documents are being added: pass next_cursor back as cursor until it comes back empty. Changing sort invalidates a cursor — request the first page again (a mismatch returns 400).

total counts every document the filters match, the status filter included. statusCounts deliberately ignores status while honouring q, sourceType and sourceId, so a UI can render the tabs and their counts without the active tab changing the other numbers. Its all entry is therefore the same as total only when no status filter is set.

The breakdown is memoised for up to 30 seconds per filter combination (project, search, source, parent, root-only, visibility) because it costs O(project) while a page is O(1); a document uploaded in that window can be missing from the tab counts until the cache expires. The listing rows and total are never cached.

docs.title: Document status
docs.text:
processingStatus folds conversion and extraction into one state, so a client does not have to combine the two raw statuses:

Value Meaning Bucket converting File is being parsed into text processing extracting Chunks are ready, AI extraction is running processing ready_for_extraction Text and embeddings are ready; extraction has not started ready completed Text, embeddings and extraction are all done extracted conversion_failed Parsing failed failed extraction_failed AI extraction failed failed

docs.title: Browsing documents in the web UI
docs.text:
Knowledge → Documents shows the same dataset with controls on top:

  • an Upload button in the page header that opens the upload form in a dialog,
  • a stats strip with the project's document total and the per-status counts,
  • a status filter (All, Processing, Ready, Extracted, Failed) in a dropdown that keeps the active search, source and sort,
  • a source filter listing the connected data sources that own documents by name, plus an Uploaded bucket for files with no source,
  • search over file names and source URLs,
  • sorting on the Created and Updated column headers (click again to flip),
  • a Load more button that appends the next page without losing the filters.

The Source column names the origin: Uploaded for a file you uploaded, and the data source's own name (for example Product Drive) for a document imported by a connected integration. A document from a data source links to that data source's page, so you can jump straight from the row to the sync that brought it in.

The Uploaded by column names the person who uploaded the document. It is blank (—) in three cases, all of them honest gaps rather than unknown data: a document imported by a data source has no single uploader (its Source column already answers where it came from), rows written before this column existed cannot be attributed after the fact, and an upload made through an ephemeral sandbox token has no person behind it. An emt_ project or account token does carry its owner, so uploads made with one name that owner. The API returns the uploader as createdByUserId with the resolved createdByDisplayName, so a client does not have to look the name up itself.

The header count is the number of documents matching every active filter — the project total when none is set — never just the length of the current page. The stats strip and the status filter's counts describe the search and source population, so selecting a status does not shift the other numbers. On narrow screens the table is replaced by a card list carrying the same fields.

docs.title: Viewing Document Content
docs.text:
Preview the converted text content of a document:

GET /api/documents/{id}/content

Download the original file:

GET /api/documents/{id}/download

docs.title: Automatic Extraction
docs.text:
If the project has auto_extract_objects enabled, the platform runs AI extraction on every new document to populate the knowledge graph with typed objects and relationships.

You can also trigger extraction manually from the document detail view in the admin UI, or via the extraction API.

Extraction pipeline

Extraction runs asynchronously. Monitor progress via Tasks or the admin extraction panel.

docs.title: Deletion Impact
docs.text:
Before deleting a document, check what would be affected:

GET /api/documents/{id}/deletion-impact

Returns counts of chunks, embeddings, and graph objects that were sourced from this document.

Bulk impact check:

POST /api/documents/deletion-impact
{ "ids": ["doc_1", "doc_2"] }

docs.title: Deleting Documents
Chunking
docs.text:
Documents are split into overlapping text segments (chunks) for retrieval. Chunking behavior is configured per project:

Setting Description strategy recursive_character (default) or markdown_structure (splits on headings and paragraphs, keeping code, math, and table blocks intact) maxChunkSize Maximum characters per chunk overlap Character overlap between consecutive chunks parentChild markdown_structure only: store a parent chunk per section alongside its children autoProfile Detect each document's shape (prose, markdown, code-heavy, tabular, transcript, email) and use that shape's parameters instead of the project-wide strategy/maxChunkSize/overlap

Configure with PUT /api/chunking/config, and read the effective settings back with GET /api/chunking/config. The write is a full replacement: turning autoProfile on stores the other fields as sent (they are then unused), so turning it back off lands on those stored values rather than the ones that were in force beforehand.

autoProfile is opt-in and replaces the project-wide size and strategy settings; it never blends with them. Documents with no dominant structure are split with the deployment's CHUNK_SIZE/CHUNK_OVERLAP defaults (1000/200 when unset) — not with a project-level maxChunkSize — so opting in changes nothing for plain prose unless the project had overridden those values. A read of the project's chunking configuration returns the per-shape profile table when autoProfile is on, reporting the effective prose defaults.

To re-chunk a specific document after changing the config:

POST /api/documents/{id}/recreate-chunks

The response summary reports the strategy actually used, plus autoProfile and the detected shape when auto-profile chose it. Chunk metadata records the same, so a chunk can be audited back to the rule that produced it.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide walks you through the first-time setup: creating an organization, setting up a project, inviting your team, and configuring your profile.

docs.title: 1. Create an Organization
docs.text:
An organization is the top-level tenant. All projects, members, and billing live under an org.

Admin UICLIAPI
  1. Open the admin panel and sign in.
  2. Navigate to Organizations and click New Organization.
  3. Enter a name (1–120 characters) and confirm.
memory orgs create --name "Acme Corp"

POST /api/orgs
Content-Type: application/json

{ "name": "Acme Corp" }

Response: 

{ "id": "org_abc123", "name": "Acme Corp", "createdAt": "..." }

docs.title: 2. Create a Project
docs.text:
A project is your isolated knowledge workspace. Objects, documents, agents, and branches all belong to a project.

Admin UICLIAPI
  1. Inside your organization, click New Project.
  2. Give it a name and an optional purpose description.
  3. Choose whether to enable automatic extraction — the platform will extract graph objects from every document you upload.
memory projects create --name "Product Research" --org <org-id>

POST /api/projects
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "Product Research",
  "organizationId": "org_abc123",
  "kb_purpose": "Track competitor research and product decisions"
}

docs.title: Project settings
docs.text: Field Description name Display name for the project kb_purpose Optional: describes what knowledge this project holds (used as context by AI features) auto_extract_objects If true, documents are automatically processed for entity extraction on upload chat_prompt_template Optional: custom system prompt for chat conversations in this project

docs.title: 3. Invite Team Members
docs.text:
Invite colleagues by email. They receive a link to accept the invitation and join your project or organization.

Admin UIAPI

Go to Project Settings → Members → Invite.

POST /api/invites
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "email": "colleague@example.com",
  "organizationId": "org_abc123",
  "projectId": "proj_xyz789",
  "role": "project_user"
}

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: Role Access project_admin Full project access: manage members, settings, agents, data sources project_user Read and write graph objects, documents, and chat

docs.title: Managing pending invites
docs.text:
GET /api/projects/{projectId}/invites      # list sent invites
DELETE /api/invites/{id}                   # revoke an invite

docs.title: Accepting an invite
docs.text:
When a user receives an invite email, they click the link which calls:

POST /api/invites/accept
{ "token": "<token-from-email>" }

docs.title: 4. Manage Members
docs.text:
Admin UIAPI

Go to Project Settings → Members to view and remove members.

GET    /api/projects/{projectId}/members          # list members
DELETE /api/projects/{projectId}/members/{userId} # remove a member

docs.title: 5. Set Up Your Profile
docs.text:
Update your display name and contact details.

Admin UIAPI

Click your avatar → Profile Settings.

GET /api/user/profile

PUT /api/user/profile
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "firstName": "Jane",
  "lastName": "Smith",
  "displayName": "Jane",
  "phoneE164": "+15551234567"
}

docs.title: Profile fields
docs.text: Field Description firstName / lastName Your real name displayName How your name appears to teammates phoneE164 Optional phone number in E.164 format avatarObjectKey Storage key for your avatar image (set via upload)

docs.title: What's next?
docs.text:
Now that you have an org, a project, and your team, configure a model so AI features work:

  • Configure models → ← required before agents, chat, or embeddings
  • Add documents →
  • Create graph objects →
  • Start a chat conversation →

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Integrations connect Memory to third-party services at the project or organization level. This page covers the GitHub App integration and general third-party integration management.

Data source integrations

For importing content from Gmail, Google Drive, GitHub, and similar sources, see Data Sources.

docs.title: GitHub App
docs.text: The GitHub App integration allows Memory to connect to your GitHub repositories — enabling repo-aware agents, automated knowledge extraction from code and issues, and OAuth-based repository access.

docs.title: Connect GitHub
docs.text:
Admin UIAPI

Go to Project Settings → Integrations → GitHub and click Connect.

POST /api/v1/settings/github/connect

This returns an authorization URL. Visit it to grant access via GitHub OAuth.

docs.title: OAuth callback
docs.text:
GitHub redirects back to:

GET /api/v1/settings/github/callback?code=...

The platform exchanges the code for an access token and stores it.

docs.title: CLI setup (API key mode)
docs.text:
For non-browser environments:

POST /api/v1/settings/github/cli
{ "token": "<github-personal-access-token>" }

docs.title: Check connection status
docs.text: GET /api/v1/settings/github

docs.title: Disconnect
docs.text: DELETE /api/v1/settings/github

docs.title: General Integrations
docs.text: These are named integration configurations — typically used for custom LLM backends, vector stores, or webhooks.

docs.title: List available integrations
docs.text:
GET /api/integrations/available

Returns integration types that can be configured in your project.

docs.title: List configured integrations
docs.text: GET /api/integrations

docs.title: Get an integration
docs.text: GET /api/integrations/{name}

docs.title: Create an integration
docs.text:
POST /api/integrations
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "my-integration",
  "displayName": "My Custom Backend",
  "enabled": true,
  "settings": { ... }
}

Note

Integration settings are encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM). They are never returned in API responses.

docs.title: Update an integration
docs.text:
PUT /api/integrations/{name}
{ "settings": { ... }, "enabled": true }

docs.title: Test an integration
docs.text:
Verify credentials and connectivity before saving:

POST /api/integrations/{name}/test

docs.title: Sync an integration
docs.text:
Trigger a manual sync or refresh:

POST /api/integrations/{name}/sync

docs.title: Delete an integration
docs.text: DELETE /api/integrations/{name}

docs.title: Public integration info
docs.text:
Some integrations expose a public endpoint (no auth required) for capabilities discovery:

GET /api/integrations/{name}/public

docs.title: Knowledge Graph
docs.text: The knowledge graph is the core of Memory. It stores objects (nodes) and relationships (edges) in a typed, versioned, searchable graph.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Concept Description Object A typed node in the graph (e.g. a Decision, Person, Requirement) Relationship A directed, typed edge between two objects (e.g. depends_on, authored_by) Type The schema that defines valid properties for an object or relationship CanonicalID Stable ID for an object across versions — use this to reference an object VersionID The ID of a specific version of an object (changes on every edit) Branch An isolated copy of the graph for safe editing; see Branches

CanonicalID vs VersionID

Always use canonical_id when linking objects, building queries, or storing references. The id field is the version-specific row; it changes every time the object is updated.

docs.title: Object Types
docs.text:
Types are defined by your project's installed template packs or custom type definitions. Common built-in types include:

  • Decision — architectural or strategic decisions
  • Requirement — product or technical requirements
  • Person — individuals mentioned in documents
  • Meeting — meeting records with participants and outcomes
  • Risk — identified risks with severity and mitigation

List available types for your project:

GET /api/type-registry/projects/{projectId}

docs.title: Creating Objects
docs.text:
CLIAPI 
memory graph objects create \
  --type Decision \
  --properties '{"title": "Use PostgreSQL", "status": "approved", "rationale": "Existing expertise"}' \
  --project my-project

# With a stable key for idempotent operations (skip if already exists):
memory graph objects create \
  --type Decision \
  --key "decision-use-postgresql" \
  --properties '{"title": "Use PostgreSQL", "status": "approved"}' \
  --project my-project

# --upsert creates-or-updates by key:
memory graph objects create \
  --type Decision \
  --key "decision-use-postgresql" \
  --properties '{"title": "Use PostgreSQL", "status": "approved"}' \
  --upsert --project my-project

POST /api/graph/objects
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "Decision",
  "properties": {
    "title": "Use PostgreSQL as primary database",
    "status": "approved",
    "rationale": "Team expertise and existing infrastructure"
  },
  "labels": ["architecture", "database"]
}

Response includes both id (version) and canonical_id (stable reference).

docs.title: Object fields
docs.text: Field Description type Object type name (must exist in the type registry) properties Key-value map of typed properties per the type schema labels Free-form string tags for filtering and organization status Optional status flag (e.g. draft, approved, archived) key Optional human-readable unique key within the project

docs.title: Creating Relationships
docs.text:
POST /api/graph/relationships
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "depends_on",
  "src_id": "<canonical_id of source object>",
  "dst_id": "<canonical_id of target object>",
  "properties": {
    "note": "Must be resolved before deployment"
  }
}

Relationships are directed: src → dst. Use type to describe the semantic of the edge.

docs.title: Bulk creating objects and relationships
docs.text:
For more than a handful of objects, use the batch commands instead of one API call per node:

# Objects only: a JSON array of {type, name, description, properties}
memory graph objects create-batch --file objects.json

# Objects + relationships: a subgraph with _ref/src_ref/dst_ref placeholders
memory graph objects create-batch --file subgraph.json

# Relationships only: a JSON array of {type, from, to}
memory graph relationships create-batch --file relationships.json

Both commands accept --branch <name-or-uuid> to write into a graph branch instead of the main graph. Objects are chunked to the server's per-call limit (500 for a subgraph, 100 per bulk item), and each row reports its own error instead of failing the whole batch.

create-batch on objects also reads the JSONL seed layout written by memory blueprints dump — pass the dump root, a seed/ directory, or a single .jsonl file. Records are upserted by key and relationship srcKey/dstKey endpoints are resolved after the objects are written, so dump → edit → import into a branch is a complete migration loop:

memory blueprints dump ./migration
memory graph objects create-batch --file ./migration --branch migration-review

See Branches § Bulk importing a dump into a branch.

docs.title: Updating Objects
docs.text:
PATCH /api/graph/objects/{id}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "properties": {
    "status": "superseded",
    "supersededBy": "Use CockroachDB"
  }
}

Every update creates a new version row. The previous version is preserved in history.

docs.title: Hybrid search (recommended)
docs.text:
Combines keyword, semantic, and graph structure in a single ranked result:

CLIAPI 
memory query "decisions about database architecture" --project my-project

POST /api/graph/search
{
  "query": "decisions about database architecture",
  "types": ["Decision"],
  "limit": 20
}

docs.title: Full-text search
docs.text: GET /api/graph/objects/fts?q=postgresql&types=Decision

docs.title: Vector (semantic) search
docs.text:
POST /api/graph/objects/vector-search
{
  "query": "scalability trade-offs",
  "topK": 10
}

docs.title: Filter by type, label, or status
docs.text: GET /api/graph/objects/search?type=Decision&status=approved&labels=architecture

docs.title: Viewing Object History
docs.text:
Every change is versioned. Retrieve the full revision history:

GET /api/graph/objects/{id}/history

Restore a previous version:

POST /api/graph/objects/{id}/restore
{ "versionId": "<old-version-id>" }

docs.title: Get all edges for an object
docs.text: GET /api/graph/objects/{id}/edges

docs.title: Expand a subgraph from a starting node
docs.text:
POST /api/graph/expand
{
  "objectId": "<canonical_id>",
  "depth": 2,
  "relationshipTypes": ["depends_on", "authored_by"]
}

docs.title: Traverse by relationship path
docs.text:
POST /api/graph/traverse
{
  "startId": "<canonical_id>",
  "direction": "outbound",
  "maxDepth": 3
}

docs.title: Find similar objects
docs.text: GET /api/graph/objects/{id}/similar?limit=5

docs.title: Bulk Operations
docs.text:
POST /api/graph/objects/bulk          # create multiple objects
POST /api/graph/relationships/bulk    # create multiple relationships
POST /api/graph/objects/bulk-update-status  # update status on many objects at once

docs.title: Deleting Objects
docs.text:
Deletion is soft — the object is marked deleted_at but preserved in history.

DELETE /api/graph/objects/{id}

To restore:

POST /api/graph/objects/{id}/restore

docs.title: Analytics
docs.text:
GET /api/graph/analytics/most-accessed   # objects viewed most recently
GET /api/graph/analytics/unused          # objects with no recent access

docs.title: Model Setup
docs.text: Before agents, chat, /remember, or /query can run, your project needs a generative model and an embedding model configured. This guide explains how to set them up.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Provider credentials and model selection are two separate things:

Thing What it is Where stored Provider credential API key or service account for an LLM provider Org-level (shared) or project-level (override) Model config Which specific model names to use Org-level (default) or project-level (override)

Resolution order — when an agent or query runs, the server resolves the model like this:

  1. Agent definition's own --model override (if set)
  2. Project-level model config (PUT /api/v1/projects/:projectId/model-config)
  3. Org-level model config (PUT /api/v1/organizations/:orgId/model-config)
  4. Nothing found → error: no generative model configured for project <id>

Setting up at the org level is the simplest path — all projects inherit it automatically.

docs.title: Supported Providers
docs.text: Provider slug What you need google Google AI API key google-vertex GCP project ID + location (+ optional service account key file) openai OpenAI API key (+ optional base URL for compatible endpoints) deepseek DeepSeek API key

docs.title: 1. Configure provider credentials at org level
docs.text:
# Google AI
memory provider configure google --api-key <YOUR_GOOGLE_API_KEY>

# Google Vertex AI
memory provider configure google-vertex --gcp-project <PROJECT_ID> --location us-central1

# OpenAI
memory provider configure openai --api-key <YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY>

# DeepSeek
memory provider configure deepseek --api-key <YOUR_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY>

By default, configure auto-selects recommended generative and embedding models. To specify explicitly:

memory provider configure google \
  --api-key <KEY> \
  --generative-model "google/gemini-2.5-flash" \
  --embedding-model "google/text-embedding-004"

Model names must include the provider prefix — e.g. google/gemini-2.5-flash, not gemini-2.5-flash. The prefix matches the provider slug.

docs.title: 2. Verify
docs.text:
memory provider list                          # show org + all project configs
memory provider test                          # live generate call using org config
memory provider test --project <PROJECT_ID>   # test via a specific project's config

docs.title: 3. Override at project level (optional)
docs.text:
If one project needs a different model than the org default:

memory provider configure-project deepseek \
  --api-key <KEY> \
  --generative-model "deepseek/deepseek-chat"

To revert a project back to org config:

memory provider configure-project deepseek --remove

docs.title: API
docs.text: You can also set model config directly via the REST API (useful if you are managing credentials programmatically and have already stored provider credentials separately).

docs.title: Set project model config
docs.text:
PUT /api/v1/projects/:projectId/model-config

{
  "generativeModel": "google/gemini-2.5-flash",
  "embeddingModel": "google/text-embedding-004"
}

docs.title: Set org model config
docs.text:
PUT /api/v1/organizations/:orgId/model-config

Same body shape.

docs.title: Check effective config (resolved with source)
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/projects/:projectId/model-config/effective

Response:

{
  "generativeModel": "google/gemini-2.5-flash",
  "generativeModelSource": "org",
  "embeddingModel": "google/text-embedding-004",
  "embeddingModelSource": "org"
}

generativeModelSource / embeddingModelSource values: "project", "org", or "none".

docs.title: Browse Available Models
docs.text:
memory provider models google                          # all google models
memory provider models google --type generative
memory provider models google --type embedding
memory provider models deepseek

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Error Cause Fix no generative model configured for project <id> No model config at project or org level Run memory provider configure <provider> --api-key <key> no project ID in context — cannot resolve generative model Auth context missing project ID Ensure you are calling the endpoint with a valid project-scoped API token model name has no provider prefix Model name like gemini-2.0-flash instead of google/gemini-2.0-flash Prefix the model name with the provider slug model resolver error for project <id> Provider credentials not stored or invalid Run memory provider test --project <id> to diagnose

docs.title: Full Project Init Example
docs.text: A complete sequence from zero to a working project with models configured.

docs.title: Option A — shared org credentials (recommended for teams)
docs.text:
Configure credentials once at the org level; all projects inherit them automatically.

# 1. Create org and project
memory orgs create --name "Acme Corp"
memory projects create --name "Product Research" --org-id <org-id>

# 2. Set the new project as active (writes MEMORY_PROJECT_ID to .env.local)
memory projects set "Product Research"

# 3. Configure provider at org level — auto-selects recommended models
memory provider configure google --api-key $GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY

# 4. Verify effective config for the project
memory provider list

# 5. Smoke test — runs a live generate call through the project's credential chain
memory provider test --project <project-id>

After step 3, every project in the org can run agents and embeddings without further setup.

docs.title: Option B — explicit model selection
docs.text:
When you need specific model versions rather than auto-selected defaults:

# Google AI with pinned models
memory provider configure google \
  --api-key $GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY \
  --generative-model "google/gemini-2.5-flash" \
  --embedding-model "google/text-embedding-004"

# DeepSeek for generation + Google for embeddings (split provider setup)
memory provider configure deepseek \
  --api-key $DEEPSEEK_API_KEY \
  --generative-model "deepseek/deepseek-chat"

memory provider configure google \
  --api-key $GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY \
  --embedding-model "google/text-embedding-004"

Model names must be provider-prefixed: google/gemini-2.5-flash, not gemini-2.5-flash.

docs.title: Option C — per-project override
docs.text:
When one project needs different models than the org default:

# Org uses google/gemini-2.5-flash by default
# This project should use a more capable model
memory provider configure-project google \
  --api-key $GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY \
  --generative-model "google/gemini-2.5-pro" \
  --embedding-model "google/text-embedding-004"

# Revert back to org config later
memory provider configure-project google --remove

docs.title: Check what's configured
docs.text:
# Show all org + project configs with resolved model names
memory provider list

# Show the resolved effective models for a project (with source: project/org/none)
# Via API:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  https://api.example.com/api/v1/projects/<project-id>/model-config/effective

Response: 

{
  "generativeModel": "google/gemini-2.5-flash",
  "generativeModelSource": "org",
  "embeddingModel": "google/text-embedding-004",
  "embeddingModelSource": "org"
}

If either *Source is "none", that model is not configured — agents and embeddings will fail until you set it.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Agents — create agents that use the configured model
  • Chat — run chat sessions against your knowledge graph

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Notifications inform you about activity in your projects — agent questions awaiting your response, completed background tasks, errors, and other system events.

docs.title: Document activity in your projects
docs.text:
A project's knowledge base is shared, so a document landing in it is project news. Four event keys cover the document lifecycle:

Event key When it fires Default Can you turn it off? document.uploaded a member uploads a document (POST /api/documents/upload, and once per request for /upload/batch) on yes document.version_synced a data-source sync appends a new version of a document (a source's first ingest does not notify) on yes document.extraction_completed extraction finished and its objects were merged into the graph on yes document.processing_failed an upload's parsing or extraction reached its final retry (dead letter) on no

docs.title: Who receives them
docs.text:
Every row goes to the project's members except the member whose action produced it — you are never notified about your own upload or your own extraction run. A data-source sync carries no actor, so a new version it appends reaches every member, including whoever pressed sync. Consequences worth knowing:

  • A solo project sees nothing from the three informational keys; there is nobody else to tell.
  • A batch upload arrives as one digest row (12 documents uploaded · a.pdf, b.pdf, c.pdf and 9 more) instead of one row per file.
  • An extraction that leaves objects on a staging branch for review sends extraction.review_ready, not document.extraction_completed — one row per extraction outcome, never both.

document.processing_failed is the exception to the actor rule: it is not suppressed for the person whose run failed, because that person is the one who has to act. It fires once, on the final attempt (retries do not notify), and names the stage that failed — Text extraction or Extraction.

docs.title: Turning them off
docs.text:
Project notification preferences are per user and per project:

GET /api/notifications/preferences?project_id=<project>

PUT /api/notifications/preferences
Content-Type: application/json

{ "projectId": "<project>", "eventKey": "document.uploaded", "enabled": false }

The three informational document keys are on by default and are reported with enabled: true before you save anything, so you disable what you do not want rather than opting into each key. document.processing_failed is required delivery (required: true): a stored preference for it is ignored when the row is created, because a processing run that died needs someone to look at it.

docs.title: Notification fields
docs.text: Field Description title Short heading message Full notification body severity info · warning · error · success importance important · other category Optional grouping label relatedResourceType The type of resource this notification relates to relatedResourceId UUID of the related resource actionUrl Optional deep link to the relevant UI page actionLabel Button label for the action link read Whether you have read the notification dismissed Whether you have dismissed it expiresAt Optional auto-expiry timestamp

docs.title: The web inbox
docs.text:
The bell in the top bar counts unread notifications for the scope on screen, and the inbox offers three scopes:

Scope Shows Everything (default) account events and project activity from every project you belong to Account account-scope events only — membership, permissions, invites, budget Project the active project only

Everything is the default for the inbox and for the bell on every other page, so a teammate's upload raises the bell while you are elsewhere in the app. In Everything and Account the list can be narrowed to a single project with the project filter, and each row carries a chip naming its project.

docs.title: Listing Notifications
docs.text: GET /api/notifications

docs.title: Filter by tab
docs.text:
Tab What it shows all Every non-dismissed notification important High-importance notifications only other Normal-importance notifications snoozed Notifications snoozed until a future time cleared Previously dismissed notifications 
GET /api/notifications?tab=important

docs.title: Notification Counts
docs.text:
Get the unread badge counts for the UI:

GET /api/notifications/counts
GET /api/notifications/stats

Response:

{
  "unread": 3,
  "important": 1,
  "pendingQuestions": 1
}

docs.title: Marking as Read
docs.text:
Mark a single notification as read:

PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read

Mark all as read:

POST /api/notifications/mark-all-read

docs.title: Dismissing a Notification
docs.text:
DELETE /api/notifications/{id}/dismiss

Dismissed notifications move to the cleared tab and are hidden from the default view.

docs.title: Real-Time Updates (SSE)
docs.text:
Subscribe to a server-sent event stream to receive notifications in real time without polling. There are two streams; which one carries a notification depends on its scope:

GET /api/events/stream/account        # account-scope notification events
GET /api/events/stream?projectId=<id> # that project's events
Accept: text/event-stream

The account stream carries only account-scope notifications for the calling user. Project-scope notifications — including every document lifecycle event — arrive on that project's stream, so a client that wants both opens both.

Frames are entity events, not notification events: the SSE event name is entity.created (or entity.updated) and the payload names the entity. Frames for documents, graph objects and agent runs travel on the same streams, so filter on entity:

const source = new EventSource('/api/events/stream?projectId=' + projectId);

source.addEventListener('entity.created', (event) => {
  const payload = JSON.parse(event.data);
  if (payload.entity !== 'notification') return;
  // payload.data.scope === 'project', payload.data.eventKey === 'document.uploaded'
  refreshUnreadCount();
});

The stream stays open; reconnect automatically if it drops.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
Tasks are background operations that require your attention or acknowledgment — things like import jobs that completed with warnings, data quality issues flagged by an agent, or operations that need manual resolution.

Tasks are distinct from Notifications: a notification informs you, a task requires you to act.

docs.title: Task fields
docs.text: Field Description title What the task is about description Optional details type Category of task (set by the system) status pending · resolved · cancelled sourceType What created this task (e.g. extraction_job, agent_run) sourceId ID of the originating resource metadata Additional context as JSON resolvedAt When it was resolved resolutionNotes Notes you added when resolving

docs.title: Listing Tasks
docs.text:
GET /api/tasks

List all tasks across all projects (requires elevated access):

GET /api/tasks/all

docs.title: Task Counts
docs.text:
Get counts for the sidebar badge:

GET /api/tasks/counts
GET /api/tasks/all/counts

Response:

{
  "pending": 4,
  "resolved": 12
}

docs.title: Getting a Task
docs.text: GET /api/tasks/{id}

docs.title: Resolving a Task
docs.text:
Mark a task as done — optionally add resolution notes:

POST /api/tasks/{id}/resolve
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "notes": "Reviewed and confirmed the extracted data is correct."
}

docs.title: Cancelling a Task
docs.text:
If a task is no longer relevant:

POST /api/tasks/{id}/cancel

docs.title: Common task types
docs.text: Type When it appears Data review Extraction produced objects flagged for review (needs_review: true) Import warning A data source sync completed with partially failed items Agent escalation An agent determined a human decision is required Schema conflict A type schema change conflicts with existing data
